(الواو) resumptive (قالوا) a past verb and its fāʿil (agent) (الهمزة) for the interrogative of denial (istifhām inkārī) (أإذا) an adverb of the future stripped of condition [Note: It may contain the meaning of condition, so the adverb is attached to the implied apodosis, i.e.: when we are bones.. shall we be raised?] in the position of an accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted [verb], its implied form being "أنبعث إذا كنا.." (كنّا) a past defective verb and its noun (عظاما) khabar (predicate), accusative (الواو) a conjunction (رفاتا) conjoined to the khabar, accusative (الهمزة) like the first (إنّا) a particle resembling the verb.. and (نا) is a pronoun in the position of an accusative, the noun of إنّ (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) (مبعوثون) the khabar of إنّ, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the wāw (خلقا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for — a pronoun in the position of an accusative, the noun of إنّ (اللام) the shifted lām (مبعوثون) the khabar of إنّ, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw (خلقا) mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun), for it is its synonym, i.e. "a raising" [Note: It may be a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e.: created.] [Translator's note: the source text repeats a passage here, apparently by a copying error; it is translated as written.], (جديدا) naʿt (adjective) of (خلقا), accusative.
The clause «قالوا ...» is a clause with no grammatical position, resumptive.
The implied clause «(أنبعث) ...» is in the position of an accusative, the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) [Note: If the adverb contains the meaning of condition, then the condition, its protasis and its apodosis are in the position of an accusative, the object of the saying.].
The clause «كنّا عظاما ...» is in the position of a genitive (majrūr), muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «إنّا لمبعوثون ...» has no grammatical position, a resumption confirming the object of the saying.. or it is an explanation of the object of the saying.
50- (قل) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "anta" (كونوا) a defective imperative verb.. and (الواو) is the noun of the defective verb (حجارة) the khabar of كونوا, accusative (أو) a conjunction (حديدا) conjoined to حجارة, accusative.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «كونوا ...» is in the position of an accusative, the object of the saying.
51- (أو) a conjunction (خلقا) conjoined to (حديدا), accusative (من) a preposition (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a genitive, attached to a naʿt of (خلقا), (يكبر) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "huwa" (في صدوركم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يكبر), and (كم) is muḍāf ilayhi (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition (السين) a particle of the future (يقولون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil (من) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject) (يعيدنا) an imperfect verb, nominative, and (نا) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is "huwa" (قل) like the first (الذي) a relative noun in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ [Note: or it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "معيدكم الذي فطركم" ("your restorer is the One who originated you").] and its khabar is omitted, its implied form being "يعيدكم" (فطركم) a past verb, and (كم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "huwa", and it is the resumptive pronoun (ʿāʾid) (أوّل) mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial) standing in for the adverb, accusative, attached to (فطركم), (مرّة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (فسينغضون) like فسيقولون (إلى) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (ينغضون), (رؤوسهم) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (هم) is muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) a conjunction (يقولون) like the first (متى) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative, an adverb of time, attached to an omitted fronted khabar, (هو) a detached pronoun, postposed mubtadaʾ (قل) like the first (عسى) a past defective verb, non-inflecting (jāmid), its noun being a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو", i.e. the raising (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative particle (يكون) an imperfect defective verb, accusative, its noun being a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو", i.e. the raising (قريبا) the khabar of يكون, accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يكون..) is in the position of an accusative, the khabar of عسى [Note: or it is the fāʿil of the complete (tāmm) عسى, i.e. its being near is hoped.].
The clause «يكبر ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ما).
The clause «يقولون ...» is in the position of a jussive (majzūm), the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. if you say that the spirit will return to you after death [Note: This saying of the Messenger is taken from His saying, exalted is He: كونوا حجارة.. and the implied sense is: if you were stones or iron.. then the spirit must be brought into being in you on the Day of Raising.] then they will say..
The clause «من يعيدنا ...» is in the position of an accusative, the object of the saying.
The clause «يعيدنا ...» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption.
The clause «فطركم» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
The clause «ينغضون ...» is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. if you say that to them, then they will shake..
The clause «يقولون ...» is conjoined to the clause ينغضون.
The clause «متى هو ...» is in the position of an accusative, the object of the saying.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption.
The clause «عسى أن يكون ...» is in the position of an accusative, the object of the saying.
The clause «يكون قريبا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
52- (يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, a badal (substitute) of (قريبا) [Note: because it is in the sense of (يوما قريبا) "a near day", or "at a near time".. It may also be a mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being اذكر ("remember").], (يدعوكم) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the wāw, and (كم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "huwa" (الفاء) a conjunction (تستجيبون) like يقولون (بحمده) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl of the agent of تستجيبون, by its being made to contain the meaning of تسبّحون ("you glorify").. and (الهاء) is muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) a conjunction (تظنّون) like يقولون (إن) a particle of negation (لبثتم) a past verb and its fāʿil (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr) (قليلا) mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial) standing in for the adverb, for it is its adjective, i.e. you remained a long time [Translator's note: the source says «وقتا طويلا» "a long time"; the sense of قليلا requires "a short time".].
The clause «يدعوكم ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «تستجيبون ...» is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause يدعوكم.
The clause «تظنّون ...» is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause تستجيبون.
The clause «لبثتم ...» is in the position of an accusative, filling the place of the two objects of ظنّ, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by (إن).

* Morphology:
(رفاتا): a non-derived (jāmid) noun for the parts of a crumbled thing; its pattern is فعال with ḍamma on the fāʾ, and it is singular.

* Rhetoric:
1- The interrogative of denial (al-istifhām al-inkārī):
in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «أَإِذا كُنَّا عِظاماً»; the repetition of the hamza in «أَإِنَّا لَمَبْعُوثُونَ» is to reinforce the denial, and likewise its reinforcement by إنّ, and the lām, to indicate the strength of the denial.
2- The device of settling (fann al-tamkīn) or anticipation (al-irṣād):
in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «قُلْ كُونُوا حِجارَةً أَوْ حَدِيداً أَوْ خَلْقاً مِمَّا يَكْبُرُ فِي صُدُورِكُمْ».
The reality of this device is: that the speaker prepares for his rhyme or his rhymed prose with a preparation in which the rhyme comes firmly settled in its place, stable in its resting place, neither jarring nor unsettled.
The hearer knows that He meant stones or iron, by a pull from his heart and an inspiration from his inner thought, without hearing the rest of the verse.
3- Incapacitating (al-taʿjīz) and humiliation (al-ihāna) in the command: «قُلْ كُونُوا حِجارَةً أَوْ حَدِيداً».

* Benefits:
- The characteristics of عسى, and likewise اخلولق and أوشك: these three verbs are distinguished in that they may be complete (tāmm), so they do not need a khabar; that is when «أن and the verb» follow them, and the maṣdar is interpreted as their fāʿil, as in: عسى أن تقوم، واخلولق أن تسافروا، وأوشك أن نرحل; and from it is the saying of Allah the Exalted: عَسى أَنْ تَكْرَهُوا شَيْئاً وَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ وَعَسى أَنْ تُحِبُّوا شَيْئاً وَهُوَ شَرٌّ لَكُمْ, and عَسى أَنْ يَبْعَثَكَ رَبُّكَ مَقاماً مَحْمُوداً. This is when no noun precedes them which is the subject of predication (musnad ilayhi) in meaning; if a noun precedes them to whose pronoun they can be predicated, you have the choice between two things:
a- To make them complete, and that is the more eloquent, so the interpreted maṣdar is their fāʿil, as in:
علي عسى أن يذهب، وهند عسى أن تذهب، والرجلان عسى أن يذهبا والمسافرون عسى أن يذهبوا, with عسى stripped of the pronoun.
b- To make them defective (nāqiṣ), so that their noun is an overt or latent pronoun, agreeing with what precedes them in singular, dual or plural, and masculine or feminine, as in: الرجلان عسيا أن يذهبا، والمرأتان عستا أن تذهبا. It is preferable in the like of that to make them complete and strip them of the pronoun, so they remain in the masculine singular form, and their fāʿil is the first [Translator's note: so in the source, «المصدر الأول»; perhaps «المؤوّل», "interpreted", is meant] maṣdar made of أن and the verb. This is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz, in which the Noble Qur'an was revealed.
عسى is distinguished by two things:
a- The permissibility of kasra and fatḥa on its sīn when it is attached to the pronoun tāʾ, the nūn of the feminine plural, or «نا»; fatḥa is preferable because it is the original. ʿĀṣim read «فهل عسيتم إن توليتم» with kasra on the sīn, and the rest read عسيتم with fatḥa. [Translator's note: the kasra reading is usually attributed to Nāfiʿ; the source attributes it to ʿĀṣim.]
b- That it may be a particle with the meaning of «لعلّ», so it acts as لعلّ does, putting the noun in the accusative and the khabar in the nominative; that is when it is attached to an accusative pronoun, and that is rare. As in the saying of the poet:
فقلت عساها نار كأس وعلّها ... تشكّى فآتي نحوها فأعودها
فتسمع قولي قبل حتف يصيبني ... تسرّ به أو قبل حتف يصيدها
(So I said: perhaps it is Kaʾs's fire, and perhaps she is ill, so I come to her and visit her; and she hears my words before a death that strikes me, and is gladdened by them — or before a death that seizes her.)

safi-cedvel:101-104.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied (muqaddar) oath; (قد) a particle of realization (taḥqīq); (آتينا) a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); (موسى) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the implied fatḥa; (تسع) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (آيات) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (بيّنات) a naʿt (adjective) of (تسع), accusative [Note: or a naʿt of آيات, genitive.], the sign of the accusative being the kasra; (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (اسأل) an imperative verb; the fāʿil is «أنت» [Note: the address is to the Messenger, upon him be peace; this is the choice of Ibn Kathīr... al-Suyūṭī also allows the address to be to Mūsā, upon him be peace, according to the difference in interpretation.]; (بني) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ, as it is treated like the sound masculine plural; (إسرائيل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa, as it is a diptote [Note: the second object is omitted, i.e. "ask them about them, O Muḥammad, a question seeking acknowledgement, to establish the proof against them".]; (إذ) an adverb of past time, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (آتينا) [Note: or attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being: "We said to him — i.e. Mūsā —: ask Pharaoh for the Children of Israel — i.e. demand them from him — when he came to them — i.e. Mūsā —"... and there is iltifāt (shift of person) in the speech. Al-ʿUkbarī allowed it to be an adverbial noun serving as mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being «اذكر».]; (جاءهم) a past verb... and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «هو», i.e. Mūsā; (الفاء) a conjunction; (قال) like جاء; (اللام) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (قال); (فرعون) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ), denied nunation for being a proper name and foreign; (إنّي) a particle resembling the verb... and (الياء) is in the position of accusative as the noun of إنّ; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis; (أظنّك) an imperfect verb, nominative... and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; the fāʿil is «أنا»; (يا) a vocative particle; (موسى) the one addressed (munādā), a singular proper name, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of accusative; (مسحورا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The clause «آتينا ...» has no grammatical position: the response to the implied oath... and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «اسأل ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "when the Children of Israel come to you, ask them about the nine signs"... [Note: or it is the speech reported by an implied verb of saying, according to the second account of the pronoun of اسأل, i.e. "We said to him: ask..."] and the clause of the condition and its apodosis has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
The clause «جاءهم ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قال له فرعون» is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause جاءهم.
The clause «إنّي لأظنّك ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported by the verb of saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أظنّك ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The vocative clause «يا موسى ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
102- (قال) a past verb; the fāʿil is «هو», i.e. Mūsā; (لقد علمت) like «لقد آتينا»; (ما) negative; (أنزل) like قال; (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (أولاء) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (ربّ) fāʿil, nominative; (السموات) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الأرض) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to السموات by the wāw, genitive; (بصائر) a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, its governing element being implied after إلّا [Note: i.e. "He sent them down as insights". This is the position of the majority, who do not allow what precedes (إلّا) to govern what follows it... Ibn ʿAṭiyya, al-Ḥawfī and Abū al-Baqāʾ al-ʿUkbarī allow such government, so بصائر is a ḥāl of (هؤلاء), the governing element being the overt أنزل.]; (الواو) a conjunction; (إنّي لأظنّك.. مثبورا) like «إنّي لأظنّك.. مسحورا».
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «علمت» has no grammatical position: the response to an implied oath... and the implied oath clause is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «ما أنزل ...» is in the position of accusative as the object of the verb of knowing, which has been suspended from direct government by the negation.
The clause «إنّي لأظنّك ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl clause.
The clause «أظنّك ...» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The vocative clause «يا فرعون» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
103- (الفاء) a conjunction; (أراد) like قال, the fāʿil being Pharaoh; (أن) a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle; (يستفزّهم) an imperfect verb, accusative... and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; the fāʿil is «هو»; (من الأرض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يستفزّهم) by making it carry the sense of «يخرجهم» ("to drive them out"); (الفاء) a conjunction; (أغرقناه) like آتينا... and (الهاء) mafʿūl bihi; (الواو) a conjunction; (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative, conjoined to the object pronoun; (مع) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to the omitted ṣila of من, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (جميعا) a ḥāl, accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يستفزّهم) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi.
The clause «أراد ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause «قال ...».
The clause «يستفزّهم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The clause «أغرقناه ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause أراد.
104- (الواو) a conjunction; (قلنا) like آتينا; (من بعده) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (قلنا), and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (لبني) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (قلنا), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ; (إسرائيل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa; (اسكنوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn... and (الواو) is the fāʿil; (الأرض) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الفاء) a conjunction; (إذا) an adverb of future time, indeclinable, in the position of accusative, attached to (جئنا); (جاء) an indeclinable past verb; (وعد) fāʿil, nominative; (الآخرة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (جئنا) like آتينا; (الباء) a preposition, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (جئنا); (لفيفا) a ḥāl, accusative, from the genitive pronoun in (بكم), i.e. "gathered together".
The clause «قلنا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause أغرقناه.
The clause «اسكنوا ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «جاء وعد ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «جئنا بكم ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.

* Morphology:
(مثبورا): a passive participle of the triliteral (ثبر); its wazn is مفعول.
(لفيفا): a collective noun (ism jamʿ) meaning "a great assembly of diverse mixtures"; its wazn is فعيل. Or it is the maṣdar of لفّ يلفّ, of the pattern-class نصر, i.e. "to join some of it to some other".

* Benefits:
- There has been disagreement about these nine signs:
The most important things to be drawn from this disagreement are two views. The first of them:
that two Jews came to Muḥammad ﷺ and asked him about the words of the Exalted «وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا مُوسى تِسْعَ آياتٍ بَيِّناتٍ», and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not associate anything with Allah; do not commit fornication; do not kill the soul that Allah has made sacred except by right; do not steal; do not practise sorcery; do not take an innocent person to the ruler so that he kills him; do not consume usury; do not slander a chaste woman; and do not flee from the battle-advance. Then he said: And upon you in particular, O Jews, that you do not transgress on the Sabbath." So they kissed his hands and feet and said: "We bear witness that you are a prophet....!"
The second of them, from Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk, is that the nine signs are:
the staff, the hand, the tongue, the sea, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood, signs made distinct... There are partial disagreements about some of the signs, which we pass over for fear of prolixity and lengthiness; the books of exegesis are before you, and in them every diligent seeker has a share.

safi-cedvel:105-106.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (بالحقّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ in (أنزلناه) [Note: i.e. "We sent it down bound up with the truth"... or "bound up", i.e. "with the truth with Us"; it may also be attached to (أنزلناه), i.e. "for the sake of establishing the truth".] or of the fāʿil (agent); (أنزلناه) a past verb and its fāʿil... and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الواو) a conjunction; (بالحقّ) like the first [Note: or attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being «آتيناك», indicated by His words «ولقد آتينا موسى..», and the clause فرقناه is a naʿt (adjective) of (قرآنا). [Translator's note: this note appears to belong with (قرآنا) in verse 106; it is placed here in the source.]; (نزل) a past verb; the fāʿil is «هو», i.e. the Qur'an; (الواو) a conjunction; (ما) negative; (أرسلناك) like أنزلناه; (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (مبشّرا) a ḥāl, accusative (manṣūb), from the second-person pronoun; (نذيرا) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to (مبشّرا) by the wāw, accusative.
The clause «أنزلناه ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «نزل ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «أرسلناك ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
106- (الواو) a conjunction; (قرآنا) mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb explained by what follows [Note: and it cannot be a ḥāl except of the pronoun referring to the Qur'an alone.]; (فرقناه) like أنزلناه; (اللام) causal (taʿlīl); (تقرأه) an imperfect verb, accusative by an «أن» concealed after the lām... and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; the fāʿil is «أنت»; (على الناس) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تقرأه); (على مكث) a preposition and its genitive noun, a ḥāl of the fāʿil of تقرأ, i.e. "unhurriedly".
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تقرأه..) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (فرقناه).
(الواو) the wāw of ḥāl; (نزّلناه) like أنزلناه; (تنزيلا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative.
The clause «(فرقنا) قرآنا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause أنزلناه.
The clause «فرقناه ...» has no grammatical position: explicative (tafsīriyya).
The clause «تقرأه ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the concealed particle-relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī) (أن).
The clause «نزّلناه ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, with (قد) implied.

* Morphology:
(مكث): a heard (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the triliteral verb مكث, of the pattern-class نصر, meaning "prolonging in duration"; its wazn is فعل with ḍamma then sukūn; it also comes with fatḥa, and it has been read so, and with kasra, though it has not been read so.
(تنزيلا): a regular (qiyāsī) maṣdar of the quadriliteral verb نزّل; its wazn is تفعيل.

* Rhetoric:
1- Explicit mention (al-dhikr), or explicitness (al-taṣrīḥ):
In the words of the Exalted: «وَبِالْحَقِّ أَنْزَلْناهُ وَبِالْحَقِّ نَزَلَ».
Had the overt noun been abandoned in favour of a pronoun, as the context would require, saying:
«وبالحق أنزلناه وبه نزل», it would not have had the grandeur it has now. Some call this al-taṣrīḥ (explicitness).
2- The art of digression (al-istiṭrād):
In the words of the Exalted «وَبِالْحَقِّ أَنْزَلْناهُ وَبِالْحَقِّ نَزَلَ».
It is a return to describing the state of the noble Qur'an, so it is connected with the words of the Exalted «لَئِنِ اجْتَمَعَتِ الْإِنْسُ وَالْجِنُّ», the verse. Such is the way of the Arabs in their speech: they take up one thing, digress from it to another, then to another, then to another, and then return to what they mentioned first.
3- Restriction (al-qaṣr):
In the words of the Exalted «وَما أَرْسَلْناكَ إِلَّا مُبَشِّراً وَنَذِيراً».
In the speech there is relative restriction (qaṣr iḍāfī). Restriction is: assigning one thing exclusively to another, by a specific means.
It is divided into real (ḥaqīqī) and relative (iḍāfī). The real is that in which the exclusiveness is according to fact and reality, not in relation to something else, as in «لا كاتب في المدينة إلا علي» ("there is no scribe in the city except ʿAlī"), when there is no other scribe in it. The relative is that in which the exclusiveness is in relation to a specific thing, as in «ما علي إلا قائم» ("ʿAlī is only standing"), i.e. he has the quality of standing, not the quality of sitting.

safi-cedvel:53-53.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (قل) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "anta" (لعبادي) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قل), the sign of the genitive being the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ, and (الياء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (يقولوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the answer to the request, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil (التي) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of an accusative (manṣūb), mafʿūl bihi (direct object) [Note: It is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted qualified noun, i.e.: let them say the word which is best.], (هي) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ), mubtadaʾ (subject) (أحسن) khabar (predicate), nominative (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb (الشيطان) the noun of إنّ, accusative (ينزغ) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "huwa" (بينهم) an adverb (ẓarf), accusative, attached to (ينزغ), (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (إنّ الشيطان) like the first (كان) a past defective verb, its noun being a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو" (للإنسان) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (عدوّا), the khabar of كان, accusative (مبينا) naʿt of (عدوّا), accusative.
The clause «قل ...» is a clause with no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يقولوا ...» has no grammatical position, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, not joined with the fāʾ, i.e.: if you ask them, they will say ... and the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) of (قل) is omitted, i.e. what you want to say.
The clause «هي أحسن ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (التي).
The clause «إنّ الشيطان ينزغ ...» has no grammatical position, giving the reason (taʿlīl) for (يقولوا) [Note: In reality the thing explained is omitted, known from the context, i.e.: and let them not say speech that is harsh on souls, because Satan ...].
The clause «ينزغ ...» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «إنّ الشيطان كان ...» has no grammatical position, giving the reason for (ينزغ).
The clause «كان للإنسان ...» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the second إنّ.

safi-cedvel:54-55.t:
* I'rab:
(ربّكم) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), and (كم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (أعلم) khabar (predicate), nominative (الباء) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive (majrūr), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أعلم) (إن) a conditional particle that puts into the jussive (يشأ) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil (agent) is "huwa" (يرحمكم) like يشأ, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and (كم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (أو) a conjunction (ان يشأ يعذّبكم) like إن يشأ يرحمكم (الواو) parenthetical (ما) negating (أرسلناك) a past verb and its fāʿil, and (الكاف) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (على) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (أرسلناك), (وكيلا) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb).
The clause «ربّكم أعلم ...» is a clause with no grammatical position, resumptive [Note: or it is in the position of an accusative, a badal (substitute) of the relative noun (التي), i.e. the word which is best is His saying: ربّكم أعلم.. and what lies between the badal and the one it replaces is a parenthesis.].
The clause «إن يشأ ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يرحمكم ...» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of the condition, not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «إن يشأ (the second)» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause إن يشأ (the first).
The clause «يعذّبكم ...» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of the second condition, not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «ما أرسلناك ...» has no grammatical position, parenthetical [Note: or conjoined to the resumptive clause.].
55- (الواو) a conjunction (ربّك أعلم) like ربّكم أعلم (الباء) a preposition (من) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a genitive, attached to (أعلم) (في السموات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of من (الأرض) conjoined to السموات by the wāw, genitive like it (الواو) a conjunction (اللام) the lām of oath for an implied oath (قد) a particle of verification (taḥqīq) (فضّلنا) a past verb and its fāʿil (بعض) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (النبيّين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ (على بعض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (فضّلنا), (الواو) a conjunction (آتينا) like فضّلنا (داود) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, barred from tanwīn because of being a proper name and foreign (ʿujma) (زبورا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The clause «ربّك أعلم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ربّكم أعلم.
The clause «قد فضّلنا ...» has no grammatical position, the answer to the implied oath.. and the implied oath clause is conjoined to the clause ربّك أعلم, with no grammatical position.
The clause «آتينا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause that answers the oath.

* Morphology:
(زبورا): the Book that was sent down to David; its pattern is فعول, either in the sense of the passive participle, like حلوب, or it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in its sense, like القبول. It is read with fatḥa and with ḍamma on the zāy, and it came in the indefinite form because it is one book among the books.

safi-cedvel:56-57.t:
* I'rab:
(قل) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "anta" (ادعوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb), mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (زعمتم) a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn.. and (تم) is a pronoun, fāʿil..
and the two objects of the verb are omitted, i.e. you claimed them to be gods (من دون) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the relative (الذين) [Note: The governor of the ḥāl is the verb ادعوا.. It is far-fetched to attach the preposition to a ḥāl of the implied first object, because the governor would then become the verb زعمتم, and the polytheists did not claim the gods to be worshipped apart from Allah, but rather [claimed] that they are partners with Him.].. and (الهاء) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition (لا) negating (يملكون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and (الواو) is the fāʿil (كشف) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (الضرّ) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) (عن) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to the maṣdar كشف (الواو) a conjunction (لا) redundant (zāʾida), for emphasizing the negation (تحويلا) conjoined to كشف, accusative.
The clause «قل ...» is a clause with no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «ادعوا ...» is in the position of an accusative, the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «زعمتم ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «لا يملكون ...» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هم"..
and the nominal clause is in the position of a jussive (majzūm), the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the implied condition, i.e. if you call them, then they do not possess.
57- (أولئك) a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ [Note: The reference is to the rational gods, such as Jesus, ʿUzayr and the angels.. and the non-rational ones.], (الذين) a relative noun in the position of a nominative, badal (substitute) of the demonstrative — or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) — (يدعون) like يملكون, and the resumptive pronoun of the relative is omitted, i.e. they call them gods (يبتغون) like يملكون (إلى ربهم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يبتغون), (الوسيلة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (أيّهم) a relative noun, indeclinable on ḍamma, in the position of a nominative, badal of the agent of يبتغون [Note: The interpreted (أيّ) came indeclinable because it is annexed and the head of its ṣila has been omitted.. It may be an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is أقرب.].. and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (أقرب) the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "هو", nominative (الواو) a conjunction in both places (يرجون رحمته، يخافون عذابه) like يملكون كشف الضرّ (إنّ) a particle of emphasis and accusative (عذاب) the noun of إنّ, accusative (ربّك) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (الكاف) is muḍāf ilayhi (كان) a past defective verb, its noun being a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو" (محذورا) khabar, accusative.
The clause «أولئك الذين ...» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «يدعون ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «يبتغون ...» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك) [Note: The clause may be a ḥāl of the agent of يدعون if the khabar of the mubtadaʾ is the relative (الذين).
(4, 5) or in the position of an accusative.].
The clause «(هو) أقرب ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (أيّ).
The clause «يرجون ...» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause يبتغون «4».
The clause «يخافون ...» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause يبتغون «5».
The clause «إنّ عذاب ...» has no grammatical position, giving the reason (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «كان محذورا ...» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of إنّ.

* Morphology:
(كشف): an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the triliteral verb كشف; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(تحويلا): a regular (qiyāsī) maṣdar of the quadriliteral verb حوّل; its pattern is تفعيل.
(يبتغون): it contains a change by deletion (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf) and a change by quiescence (iʿlāl bi-l-taskīn); its original form is يبتغيون — with ḍamma on the second yāʾ — the ḍamma was felt heavy on the yāʾ, so it was moved to the ghayn and the yāʾ was made quiescent — iʿlāl bi-l-taskīn — then the yāʾ was dropped because it met, quiescent, with the wāw of the plural, so it became يبتغون; its pattern is يفتعون.
(محذورا): a passive participle from the triliteral حذر; its pattern is مفعول.

* Benefits:
- أَيُّهُمْ أَقْرَبُ.
The grammarians summarized the ways in which «أي» comes, and they were six:
1- Conditional: «أَيًّا ما تَدْعُوا فَلَهُ الْأَسْماءُ الْحُسْنى», as shown by the jussive of تدعو and the entry of the linking fāʾ in its apodosis.
2- Interrogative: «أَيُّكُمْ زادَتْهُ هذِهِ إِيماناً»..?
3- Relative: «لَنَنْزِعَنَّ مِنْ كُلِّ شِيعَةٍ أَيُّهُمْ أَشَدُّ».
4- Indicating perfection, as in: زيد رجل أي رجل? ("Zayd is a man — what a man!")
5- Being a link for addressing in the vocative what has «ال», as in: يا أيها الرجل.
6- Being for exclamation: سبحان الله أي رجل هذا! ("Glory be to Allah, what a man this is!") It is declinable (muʿrab) in all its states, except when it is relative, annexed, and the head of its ṣila is omitted, in which case it is indeclinable on ḍamma. It has detailed treatment in the extensive works.

safi-cedvel:58-59.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (إن) negating (من) redundant (zāʾida) (قرية) genitive (majrūr) in form, nominative (marfūʿ) in position, mubtadaʾ (subject) (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr) (نحن) a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ (مهلكوها) khabar (predicate), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.. and (ها) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (قبل) an adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (مهلكوها), (يوم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (القيامة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (أو) a conjunction (معذّبوها) conjoined to (مهلكوها), parsed like it (عذابا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative, its governor being the active participle معذوبها [Translator's note: so spelled in the source; معذّبوها is meant] (شديدا) naʿt (adjective) of (عذابا), accusative (كان ... مسطورا) like كان محذورا [Note: in the preceding verse (57).], (ذلك) a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a nominative, the noun of كان.. and (اللام) is for distance and (الكاف) for address (في الكتاب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (مسطورا).
The clause «إن من قرية ...» is a clause with no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «نحن مهلكوها ...» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (قرية).
The clause «كان ذلك ... مسطورا» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
59- (الواو) a conjunction (ما) negating (منعنا) a past verb, and (نا) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative particle (نرسل) an imperfect verb, accusative, and the fāʿil (agent) is "naḥnu", for majesty (بالآيات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the implied object of نرسل, i.e. "We send a prophet bearing the signs" [Note: The bāʾ may be a redundant preposition.. and الآيات the object of نرسل.]; and the interpreted maṣdar (أن نرسل ...) is in the position of a genitive by an omitted preposition, attached to (منعنا), i.e. "prevented Us from sending" (إلّا) a particle of restriction (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle (كذّب) a past verb (الباء) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (كذّب), (الأوّلون) fāʿil, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن كذّب ...) is in the position of a nominative, the fāʿil of منع (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya) (آتينا) a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn.. and (نا) is a pronoun, fāʿil (ثمود) first mafʿūl bihi, accusative, barred from tanwīn because of being a proper name and foreign (ʿujma) [Translator's note: so in the source; ثمود is usually treated as a diptote for being a proper name and feminine (a tribe).] (الناقة) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (مبصرة) ḥāl, accusative (الفاء) a conjunction (ظلموا) a past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil (الباء) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (ظلموا) by its being made to contain the meaning of كفروا ("they disbelieved") (الواو) a conjunction (ما) negating (نرسل بالآيات) like the first, and the verb is nominative.. (إلّا) like the first (تخويفا) mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative [Note: It may be a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl of the agent, i.e. "warning" — مخوّفين with kasra on the wāw — or of the object, i.e. "warned by them".].
The clause «ما منعنا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause إن من قرية ...
The clause «نرسل ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أنّ) [Translator's note: so in the source, with shadda; أن is meant].
The clause «كذّب بها الأوّلون ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the second particle-relative (أن).
The clause «آتينا ...» has no grammatical position, parenthetical [Note: or in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl, with (قد) implied.].
The clause «ظلموا بها ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the parenthetical clause.
The clause «ما نرسل بالآيات إلّا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause منعنا.

* Morphology:
(مهلكوها): in the plural form for majesty; its singular is مهلك.. see verse (164) of Sūrat al-Aʿrāf.
(معذّبوها): in the plural form for majesty; its singular is معذّب.. see verse (164) of Sūrat al-Aʿrāf.
(مسطورا): a passive participle from the triliteral سطر; its pattern is مفعول.
(تخويفا): a regular (qiyāsī) maṣdar of the quadriliteral verb خوّف; its pattern is تفعيل.

* Rhetoric:
1- Figurative attribution (al-isnād al-majāzī):
in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «وَما مَنَعَنا أَنْ نُرْسِلَ بِالْآياتِ».
Prevention is impossible with respect to Him, exalted is He, because nothing prevents Allah from His will. So "prevention" is a figure for "leaving off", i.e. the cause of leaving off the sending of the signs was nothing but the denial of the earlier peoples.
2- Rational figure (al-majāz al-ʿaqlī):
in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «النَّاقَةَ مُبْصِرَةً».
Since the she-camel was a cause of seeing the truth and guidance, seeing was attributed to her; so there is a majāz ʿaqlī in it, whose relation is causality.

safi-cedvel:107-109.t:
* I'rab:
(قل) an imperative verb; the fāʿil (agent) is «أنت»; (آمنوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn... and (الواو) is the fāʿil; (الباء) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (آمنوا); (أو) a conjunction; (لا) the jussive lā of prohibition; (تؤمنوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn... and (الواو) is the fāʿil, and the second (به) is implied (muqaddar); (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as the noun of إنّ; (أوتوا) a past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma, passive... and (الواو) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (العلم) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (من قبله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أوتوا), and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (إذا) an adverb of future time containing the sense of condition, indeclinable, in the position of accusative, attached to the apodosis يخرّون; (يتلى) an imperfect verb, passive... and the nāʾib fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being «هو», i.e. the Qur'an; (على) a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (يتلى); (يخرّون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ)... and (الواو) is the fāʿil; (للأذقان) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يخرّون) by making it carry the sense of «يذلّون» ("they humble themselves") [Note: or the lām means «على», i.e. "they fall upon their faces"... The preposition phrase may also be attached to (سجّدا).]; (سجّدا) a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا به ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported by the verb of saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «لا تؤمنوا ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the maqūl al-qawl clause.
The clause «إنّ الذين أوتوا ...» has no grammatical position: causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «أوتوا العلم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «the condition, its verb and its apodosis» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «يتلى ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «يخرّون ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
108- (الواو) a conjunction — or circumstantial (ḥāliyya) —; (يقولون) like يخرّون; (سبحان) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb; (ربّنا) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr)... and (نا) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (إن) lightened from the heavy (إنّ), necessarily inoperative; (كان) a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) —; (وعد) the noun of كان, nominative; (ربّنا) like the first; (اللام) the distinguishing lām (al-fāriqa); (مفعولا) the khabar of كان, accusative.
The clause «يقولون ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يخرّون [Note: or it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of يخرّون, i.e. "they fall down while saying..."].
The clause «(نسبح) سبحان ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical, of supplication.
The clause «كان وعد ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl.
109- (الواو) a conjunction; (يخرّون للأذقان) like the first; (يبكون) like يخرّون; (الواو) a conjunction — or circumstantial —; (يزيدهم) an imperfect verb, nominative... and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; the fāʿil is «هو», i.e. the Qur'an, or the weeping, or the prostration...; (خشوعا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The clause «يخرّون (the second)» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يخرّون (the first).
The clause «يبكون ...» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of يخرّون.
The clause «يزيدهم ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause يبكون [Note: or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of يبكون.].

* Morphology:
(الأذقان): plural of ذقن, a non-derived (jāmid) noun for the well-known body part (the chin); its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn, and the wazn of أذقان is أفعال.
(خشوعا): a heard (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the triliteral verb خشع, of the pattern-class فتح; its wazn is فعول with ḍamma on the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:110-111.t:
* I'rab:
(قل ادعوا) like «قل آمنوا» [Note: in verse (107) of this sūra.]; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (أو) a conjunction; (ادعوا الرحمن) like «ادعوا الله»; (أيّا) a jussive conditional noun, mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb); (ما) redundant (zāʾida); (تدعوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn... and (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent); (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (اللام) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a khabar (predicate) placed first; (الأسماء) a mubtadaʾ (subject) placed after, nominative (marfūʿ); (الحسنى) a naʿt (adjective) of الأسماء, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (الواو) a conjunction; (لا) the jussive lā of prohibition; (تجهر) an imperfect verb, jussive; the fāʿil is «أنت»; (بصلاتك) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تجهر), and (الكاف) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الواو) a conjunction; (لا تخافت) like «لا تجهر»; (الباء) a preposition, and (ها) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (تخافت); (الواو) a conjunction; (ابتغ) an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the weak letter; the fāʿil is «أنت»; (بين) an adverb, accusative, attached to (سبيلا) [Note: or attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (سبيلا) — an adjective placed before what it qualifies —.], which is the mafʿūl bihi.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ادعوا الله ...» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported by the verb of saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «ادعوا الرحمن ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause «ادعوا الله».
The clause «تدعوا ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «له الأسماء ...» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «لا تجهر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause قل.
The clause «لا تخافت ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause «لا تجهر».
The clause «ابتغ ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause «لا تجهر».
111- (الواو) a conjunction; (قل) like the first; (الحمد) mubtadaʾ, nominative; (لله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; (الذي) a relative, in the position of genitive as a naʿt of the Name of Majesty; (لم) a particle of negation and of the jussive; (يتّخذ) an imperfect verb, jussive; the fāʿil is «هو»; (ولدا) second mafʿūl bihi [Note: the first object is implied, i.e. "He has not taken anyone as a son".], accusative; (الواو) a conjunction; (لم) like the first; (يكن) a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive; (له) like the first, attached to the khabar of كان; (شريك) the noun of كان, nominative; (في الملك) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (شريك); (الواو) a conjunction; (لم يكن له وليّ) like «لم يكن له شريك»; (من الذلّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (وليّ), and من is causal, i.e. "on account of humiliation"; (الواو) a conjunction; (كبّره) an imperative verb... and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; the fāʿil is «أنت»; (تكبيرا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause «قل ادعوا ...».
The clause «الحمد لله ...» is in the position of accusative as maqūl al-qawl.
The clause «لم يتّخذ ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذي).
The clause «لم يكن له شريك ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «لم يكن له وليّ ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «كبّره ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause «قل..».

* Morphology:
(ابتغ): it contains iʿlāl by deletion, in conformity with the indeclinable (imperative) form; its wazn is افتع.
(تكبيرا): a regular (qiyāsī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the quadriliteral verb كبّر; its wazn is تفعيل.

* Benefits:
1- The Most Beautiful Names of Allah:
The jurists are agreed that Allah has ninety-nine names, and they are as follows:
هو الله الذي لا إله إلا هو الرحمن الرحيم الملك القدوس السلام المؤمن المهيمن العزيز الجبار المتكبر الخالق البارئ المصور الغفار القهار الوهاب الرزاق الفتاح العليم القابض الباسط الخافض الرافع المعز المذل السميع البصير الحكم العدل اللطيف الخبير الحليم العظيم الغفور الشكور العلي الكبير الحفيظ المقيت الحسيب الخليل [Translator's note: so printed; the well-known list has «الجليل» here.] الكريم الرقيب المجيب الواسع الحكيم الودود المجيد الباعث الشهيد الحق الوكيل القوي المتين الولي الحميد المحصي المبدئ المعيد المحيي المميت الحي القيوم الواجد الماجد الواحد الأحد الصمد القادر المقتدر المقدم المؤخر الأول الآخر الباطن الظاهر الوالي المتعالي البر التواب المنتقم العفو الرؤوف، مالك الملك ذو الجلال والإكرام المقسط الجامع الغني المغني المانع الضار النافع النور الهادي البديع الباقي الوارث الرشيد الصبور.
2- The bewilderment of Quraysh before the Qur'an:
Among what history has preserved for us is that Abū Jahl, Abū Sufyān and al-Akhnas went out one night to listen to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was praying at night in his house. Each of them took a place to listen in, without his two companions seeing him. They spent the night listening until dawn broke; they dispersed, and the road brought them together. They blamed one another, and some said to others: "Do not go back to the like of this; if your foolish ones saw you, you would plant something in their souls." Then they departed. When the second night came, they went back to what they had done the previous night. Then they departed and met on the road, and said what they had said the first time. When the third night came, they went back and listened, then departed, met and reproached one another, and then made a pact not to go back to the like of it....!
When morning came, al-Akhnas took his staff and went out until he came to Abū Sufyān in his house, and said to him: "Tell me, O Abū Ḥanẓala, your opinion of what you heard." He said: "O Abū Thaʿlaba, by Allah, I heard things that I recognize and know what is meant by them, and I heard things whose meaning I did not know, nor what is meant by them." Al-Akhnas said:
"And I, by the One by whom I swore, am the same."
Then he left him and came to Abū Jahl, and said to him: "O Abū al-Ḥakam, what is your opinion of what you heard from Muḥammad?" He said: "What did I hear? We and the Banū ʿAbd Manāf contended for honour: they fed, so we fed; they gave, so we gave; until, when we were knee to knee and were like two racehorses, they said:
'From us is a prophet to whom revelation comes from heaven.' So when shall we attain the like of this... By Allah, we will never believe in him nor accept him as truthful"

safi-cedvel:60-60.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (إذ) an adverbial noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of an accusative (manṣūb), mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being اذكر ("remember") (قلنا) a past verb and its fāʿil (agent) (اللام) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of a genitive (majrūr) (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — (ربّك) the noun of إنّ, accusative, and (الكاف) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (أحاط) a past verb, and the fāʿil is "huwa" (بالناس) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أحاط), (الواو) a conjunction (ما) negating (جعلنا) like قلنا (الرؤيا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif (التي) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative, naʿt (adjective) of الرؤيا (أريناك) like قلنا..
and (الكاف) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, (إلا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr) (فتنة) second mafʿūl bihi of the verb جعلنا, accusative (للناس) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt of (فتنة) [Note: or attached to فتنة.. or it is the lām of strengthening (lām al-taqwiya), redundant (zāʾida), and the noun it puts in the genitive is in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi.], (الشجرة) conjoined to الرؤيا by the wāw, accusative (الملعونة) naʿt of الشجرة, accusative (في القرآن) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (الملعونة) (الواو) a conjunction (نخوّفهم) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and (هم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "naḥnu", for majesty (الفاء) a conjunction (ما) negating (يزيدهم) an imperfect verb, nominative, and (هم) is like the last, and the fāʿil is "huwa", i.e. the warning (إلّا) like the first (طغيانا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (كبيرا) naʿt of (طغيانا), accusative.
The clause «قلنا ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «إنّ ربّك ...» is in the position of an accusative, the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أحاط ...» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «ما جعلنا ...» is a clause with no grammatical position, conjoined to the implied resumptive clause, namely the clause اذكر.
The clause «أريناك ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (التي).
The clause «نخوّفهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «ما يزيدهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause نخوّفهم.

* Morphology:
(الرؤيا): it is sight with the eyes, not a dream-vision, because this seeing took place when the noble Messenger was taken by night and ascended to heaven, and that happened while awake, not in sleep.
(الملعونة): feminine of الملعون, a passive participle from the triliteral لعن; its pattern is مفعولة.

safi-cedvel:61-61.t:
* I'rab:
(وإذ قلنا للملائكة) like وإذ قلنا لك [Note: in the preceding verse (60).], (اسجدوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent) (لآدم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (اسجدوا), the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa (الفاء) a conjunction (سجدوا) a past verb and its fāʿil (إلّا) for exception (إبليس) excepted by إلّا, accusative (manṣūb) by way of the disconnected (munqaṭiʿ) or connected (muttaṣil) exception (قال) a past verb, and the fāʿil is "huwa" (الهمزة) for interrogation, (أسجد) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "أنا" (اللام) a preposition (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of a genitive (majrūr), attached to (أسجد) (خلقت) a past verb and its fāʿil (طينا) accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "from clay" [Note: al-ʿUkbarī allowed it to be a ḥāl (circumstantial) despite its being non-derived (jāmid), because of the meaning of origin it contains..].
The clause «قلنا ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «اسجدوا ...» is in the position of an accusative, the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «سجدوا ...» is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause قلنا.
The clause «قال ...» is a clause with no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «أأسجد ...» is in the position of an accusative, the object of the saying.
The clause «خلقت ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).

safi-cedvel:62-67.t:
* I'rab:
(قال) a past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is a pronoun, its implied form being "هو", i.e. Satan (الهمزة) for interrogation (رأيتك) a past verb and its fāʿil ... and (الكاف) is a particle of address [Note: See further detail in the i'rab of the parallel verse in Sūrat al-Anʿām, verse (40).], i.e. "tell me" (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh) (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of an accusative (manṣūb), mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative, badal (substitute) of the demonstrative — or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) — (كرّمت) like رأيت (على) a preposition and (الياء) a pronoun in the position of a genitive (majrūr), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (كرّمت) ... and the second object is an implied interrogative clause indicated by the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative, i.e. why have You honoured him above me? 63- (قال) like the first, and the fāʿil is "huwa", i.e. Allah (اذهب) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "anta" (الفاء) a conjunction (من) a conditional noun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject) (تبعك) a past verb, and (الكاف) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "huwa", and the verb is in the position of a jussive, the protasis (من) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent (الفاء) linking the apodosis (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb (جهنّم) the noun of إنّ, accusative, barred from tanwīn because of being a proper name and feminine (جزاؤكم) the khabar (predicate) of إنّ, nominative..

64- (الواو) resumptive (استفزز) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "anta" (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (استطعت) like كرّمت (منهم) like the first, attached to a ḥāl of the omitted resumptive pronoun (ʿāʾid), i.e. whom you are able to provoke of them (بصوتك) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (استفزز).. and (الكاف) is muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) a conjunction (اجلب) like استفزز (عليهم) like منهم, attached to (اجلب), (بخيلك) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl of the agent of اجلب [Note: al-Jamal said in his marginal gloss: «In al-Mukhtār: جلب على فرسه يجلب جلبا, on the pattern طلب يطلب طلبا, means he shouted at it from behind and urged it on to race; and likewise أجلب عليه. The clause «استطعت ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (من).
The clause «اجلب ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause استفزز.
The clause «شاركهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause استفزز.
The clause «عدهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause استفزز.
The clause «يعدهم الشيطان ...» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl.
65- (إنّ عبادي) like إنّ جهنّم, and the sign of the accusative is the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ ... and (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi (ليس) a past defective verb, non-inflecting (jāmid) (اللام) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to the khabar of ليس (عليهم) like منهم, attached to the khabar [Note: or attached to an omitted ḥāl of سلطان — an adjective that has come before the noun it qualifies —] (سلطان) the noun of ليس, nominative (الواو) a conjunction (كفى) a past verb, indeclinable on the implied fatḥa (الباء) a redundant (zāʾida) preposition (ربّك) genitive in form, nominative in position, the fāʿil of كفى.. and (الكاف) is muḍāf ilayhi (وكيلا) ḥāl, accusative [Note: or tamyīz, accusative.].
The clause «إنّ عبادي ليس لك ...» has no grammatical position, a resumption within the scope of the saying.
The clause «ليس لك عليهم سلطان ...» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «كفى بربّك وكيلا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause إنّ عبادي ...
66- (ربّكم) mubtadaʾ, nominative.. and (كم) is muḍāf ilayhi (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, khabar (يزجي) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil is "huwa", which is the resumptive pronoun (اللام) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (يزجي) (الفلك) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (في البحر) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يزجي) [Note: or attached to an omitted ḥāl of الفلك.], (اللام) for giving the reason (taʿlīl) (تبتغوا) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil (من فضله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تبتغوا), and (الهاء) is muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تبتغوا ...) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to (يزجي) (إنّه) a particle resembling the verb.. and (الهاء) is the noun of إنّ (كان) a past defective verb, its noun being a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو" (بكم) like لكم, attached to (رحيما), which is the khabar of كان, accusative.
The clause «ربّكم الذي ...» has no grammatical position, a reason for the sufficiency of the power and an explanation of it.
The clause «يزجي لكم الفلك ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
The clause «تبتغوا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «إنّه كان بكم ...» has no grammatical position, a reason for His saying يزجي.
