67- (الواو) a conjunction (إذا) an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative, attached to (ضلّ), (مسّكم) a past verb ... and (كم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (الضرّ) fāʿil, nominative (في البحر) a preposition and its genitive noun, a ḥāl of the agent or of the object (ضلّ) a past verb (من) a relative noun, fāʿil, in the position of a nominative (تدعون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil (إلّا) a particle of exception (إيّاه) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative by way of the disconnected (munqaṭiʿ) or connected (muttaṣil) exception (الفاء) a conjunction (لمّا) an adverb meaning "when", containing the meaning of condition, attached to (أعرضتم), (نجّاكم) a past verb, indeclinable on the implied fatḥa.. and (كم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "huwa" (إلى البرّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (نجّاكم) by its being made to contain the meaning of أوصلكم ("brought you") (أعرضتم) a past verb and its fāʿil (الواو) resumptive (كان ... كفورا) like كان.. رحيما (الإنسان) the noun of كان, nominative.
The clause «مسّكم الضرّ ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «ضلّ من تدعون ...» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «تدعون ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative (من).
The clause «نجّاكم ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «أعرضتم ...» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of the condition (لمّا).
The clause «كان الإنسان كفورا ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(موفورا): a passive participle from the triliteral وفر; its pattern is مفعول, and it has been used in the sense of the active participle, i.e. وافرا ("abundant"), in the manner of the rational figure (majāz ʿaqlī).
(رجلك): a collective noun (ism jamʿ) meaning "footmen"; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then kasra, and the ʿayn may be made quiescent.
(عدهم): it contains a change by deletion (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf); its past is وعد, an assimilated weak verb (mithāl) with kasra on the ʿayn in the imperfect, whose fāʾ is dropped in the imperfect and the imperative; its pattern is عل with kasra on the ʿayn.
(يعدهم): the change in it is of the same kind as the change in (عدهم).

* Rhetoric:
1- The loose figure (al-majāz al-mursal):
in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «أَرَأَيْتَكَ هذَا الَّذِي كَرَّمْتَ عَلَيَّ».
This is a figure in using "seeing" in the sense of "informing", so the meaning is: tell me about this one whom You have honoured above me — why have You honoured him above me when I am nobler than he? The relation is what lies between knowledge and informing, of cause and effect, and of the entailing and the entailed.
2- The representative metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya):
in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «وَأَجْلِبْ عَلَيْهِمْ بِخَيْلِكَ وَرَجِلِكَ».
The verse represents the state of Satan: his provoking with his voice and his rallying of his horse and foot are a representation of his domination over whomever he leads astray, as though a raider fell upon a people, shouted at them with a shout that dislodged them from their places, and rallied against them his troops of horsemen and footmen until he uprooted them.
3- Shift of address (al-iltifāt):
in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «وَما يَعِدُهُمُ الشَّيْطانُ إِلَّا غُرُوراً».
Here there is a shift from the second person to the third. What the outward context required was to say: وما تعدهم إلا غرورا, but it turned away from that to strengthen the sense of the parenthesis, together with what it contains of turning the speech away from addressing him and explaining his state to people, and of intimating that his devilry is the cause of deception, which is the embellishing of error with what gives the impression that it is right.

* Benefits:
1- The mafʿūl muṭlaq is governed by one of four governors:
a- A maṣdar like it in wording and meaning, as in the verse.
b- Or a maṣdar in meaning but not in wording, as in:
«أعجبني إيمانك تصديقا» ("your faith, a believing, pleased me").
c- A verb derived from it: «وَكَلَّمَ اللَّهُ مُوسى تَكْلِيماً».
d- Or an active or passive participle used intensively, derived from its verb, as in: «وَالصَّافَّاتِ صَفًّا» or (الخبز مأكول أكلا) — the first is the intensive of the active participle, the second the intensive of the passive participle. The discussion will be completed in what is to come, Allah willing.
2- The prepared ḥāl (al-ḥāl al-muwaṭṭaʾa) is the non-derived (jāmid) noun that is mentioned and prepared for with a derived adjective so that it may be considered a ḥāl, as in: «فَتَمَثَّلَ لَها بَشَراً سَوِيًّا».
The explanation of that is: when the non-derived noun is qualified by what may be a ḥāl, it itself becomes valid as a ḥāl — so consider it carefully..!
3- The adverbial لمّا:
it is the one that means «حين ("when") or إذا» and requires two clauses whose verbs are both past.
It is in the accusative by its apodosis.
It is annexed to its first verb; in other words: the first clause is in the position of a genitive by the annexation of «لمّا» to it.
The verifying scholars hold that it is a means of linking two clauses, and for that reason they called it «the particle of existence for existence» (ḥarf wujūd li-wujūd).
That is, it indicates the existence of something because of the existence of something else. We may clarify it further in another place, Allah willing.

safi-cedvel:68-69.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for the interrogative of rebuke (istifhām tawbīkhī) (الفاء) resumptive [Note: According to the parsers it is a conjunction that conjoins the overt to something implied, i.e. were you saved from drowning and so felt secure..], (أمنتم) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn.. and (تم) is a pronoun, fāʿil (agent) (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative particle (نخسف) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and the fāʿil is "naḥnu", for majesty (الباء) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive (majrūr), attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of جانب البرّ [Note: The bāʾ may be causal, so it is attached to the verb نخسف.], (جانب) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative [Note: Some allowed it to be an adverb.. with the object implied.], (البرّ) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive; and the interpreted maṣdar (أن نخسف..) is in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (الواو) a conjunction (نرسل عليكم حاصبا) like نخسف بكم جانب and conjoined to it (ثمّ) a conjunction (لا) negating (تجدوا) an imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to the accusative (نرسل), the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil (لكم) like بكم, attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (وكيلا) first mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The clause «أمنتم ...» is a clause with no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «نخسف ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «نرسل ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause نخسف.
The clause «تجدوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause نرسل.
69- (أم) it is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) one, meaning بل and the hamza (أمنتم أن نعيدكم) like أمنتم أن نخسف.. and (كم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, (في) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (نعيدكم), (تارة) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun), for it is its synonym (أخرى) naʿt (adjective) of تارة, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن نعيدكم..) is in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (الفاء) a conjunction (نرسل عليكم قاصفا) like نرسل عليكم حاصبا, and the verb is conjoined to (نعيدكم), (من الريح) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt of (قاصفا), (الفاء) a conjunction (يفرقكم) [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has فيغرقكم, and the source itself uses يغرقكم below] an imperfect verb, accusative, conjoined to نرسل..
and (كم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "huwa" (الباء) a causal preposition (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle (كفرتم) like أمنتم.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما كفرتم..) is in the position of a genitive by the bāʾ, attached to (يغرقكم) (ثمّ لا تجدوا لكم ... تبيعا) like ثمّ لا تجدوا لكم وكيلا, and the verb is conjoined to يغرقكم (على) a preposition and (نا) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (تبيعا), (به) like بكم, attached to (تجدوا) [Note: It may be attached to (تبيعا), or to an omitted ḥāl of (تبيعا).].
The clause «أمنتم (the second) ...» has no grammatical position, resumptive [Note: (أم) may be the connected (muttaṣila) one, so the clause is conjoined to the first clause أمنتم.].
The clause «نعيدكم ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «نرسل ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause نعيدكم.
The clause «يغرقكم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause نرسل.
The clause «كفرتم ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
The clause «لا تجدوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يغرقكم.

* Morphology:
(جانب): a noun meaning "side", in the form of the active participle; its pattern is فاعل.
(حاصبا): a noun meaning the wind or the cloud; it came in the form of the active participle of the verb حصبه, of the ضرب class, i.e. he pelted him with الحصباء, which are small stones.
(قاصفا): a noun for the violent wind that smashes things and breaks them; it came on the pattern فاعل from the triliteral قصف meaning "to break", of the ضرب class.
(تبيعا): a derived word; its pattern is فعيل in the sense of فاعل, and it is one who demands a right and persists in the demand.

safi-cedvel:70-70.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (اللام) the lām of oath for an implied oath (قد) a particle of verification (taḥqīq) (كرّمنا) a past verb and its fāʿil (agent) (بني) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ (آدم) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa (الواو) a conjunction (حملناهم) like كرّمنا.. and (هم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (في البرّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object pronoun (البحر) conjoined to البرّ by the wāw, genitive (الواو) a conjunction (رزقناهم) like حملناهم (من الطيّبات) a preposition and its genitive noun, a ḥāl of the object pronoun, i.e. "eating" [Note: It may be attached to (رزقناهم) by its being made to contain the meaning of أطعمناهم ("We fed them").], (الواو) a conjunction (فضّلناهم) "hum" حملناهم [Translator's note: so in the source, «هم حملناهم»; probably «مثل حملناهم», "like حملناهم", is meant.] (على كثير) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (فضّلنا), (من) a preposition (من) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a genitive, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of كثير (خلقنا) like كرّمنا (تفضيلا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative.
The clause «كرّمنا ...» is a clause with no grammatical position, the answer to the implied oath ... and the implied oath clause has no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «حملناهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause كرّمنا.
The clause «رزقناهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause كرّمنا.
The clause «فضّلناهم ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause كرّمنا.
The clause «خلقنا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).

safi-cedvel:71-72.t:
* I'rab:
(يوم) mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being اذكر ("remember") [Note: or it is an adverb of time for an omitted verb explained by what follows, i.e. they will not be wronged on the day We call.], (ندعو) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the wāw, and the fāʿil (agent) is "naḥnu", for majesty (كلّ) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) (أناس) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) (بإمامهم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ندعو) [Note: or attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. mingled with their leader.].. and (هم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (الفاء) a conjunction (من) a conditional noun that puts into the jussive, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject) (أوتي) a past verb, passive, indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of a jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو", and it is the resumptive pronoun (كتابه) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (الهاء) is muḍāf ilayhi (بيمينه) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أوتي), and (الهاء) is like the last (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) (أولئك) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ.. and (الكاف) is for address (يقرءون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil (كتابهم) like كتابه (الواو) a conjunction (لا) negating (يظلمون) an imperfect verb, passive, nominative.. and (الواو) is the nāʾib fāʿil (فتيلا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative, standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun), for it is its adjective.
The clause «(اذكر) يوم ندعو ...» is a clause with no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «ندعو ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «من أوتي ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «أوتي كتابه ...» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: The khabar may be the protasis and apodosis clauses together.].
The clause «أولئك يقرءون» is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «يقرءون ...» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).
The clause «لا يظلمون ...» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause يقرءون.
72- (الواو) a conjunction (من) like the first (كان) a past defective verb, indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of a jussive, the protasis, its noun being a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو" (في) a preposition (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh) (ذه) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of a genitive, attached to (أعمى), which is the khabar of كان, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the implied fatḥa on the alif (الفاء) linking the apodosis (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ (في الآخرة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the second (أعمى), which is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the alif (الواو) a conjunction (أضلّ) conjoined to the khabar أعمى, nominative (سبيلا) tamyīz (specification), accusative.
The clause «من كان ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause من أوتي ...
The clause «كان ... أعمى» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «هو ... أعمى» is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.

* Morphology:
(أعمى): an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from the verb عمي يعمى, of the فرح class; its pattern is أفعل. The word may be an elative (ism tafḍīl), since the elative أضلّ comes after it..
See verse (60) of Sūrat al-Māʾida.

safi-cedvel:73-76.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (إن) lightened from the heavy [إنّ], necessarily inoperative (كادوا) a past defective verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma.. and (الواو) is the noun of كاد (اللام) it is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa) (يفتنون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent) and (الكاف) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) (عن) a preposition (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of a genitive (majrūr), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يفتنون) by its being made to contain the meaning of يصرفونك ("they turn you away") (أوحينا) a past verb and its fāʿil (إلى) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (أوحينا), (اللام) for giving the reason (taʿlīl) (تفتري) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of reason, and the fāʿil is "anta" (على) a preposition and (نا) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (تفتري), (غيره) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (الهاء) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct)..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تفتري..) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to (يفتنونك).
(الواو) a conjunction (إذا) — with tanwīn — a particle of response with no governing effect (اللام) occurring in the apodosis of an implied condition [Note: i.e.: if you had done so, they would have taken you — as is mentioned after that — al-Jamal in his marginal gloss made it the lām of oath for an implied oath, but this usually requires (قد), as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: تالله لقد آثرك الله علينا.] (اتّخذوك) a past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil, and (الكاف) is like the first in the verse (خليلا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The clause «كادوا ...» is a clause with no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «يفتنونك ...» is in the position of an accusative, the khabar (predicate) of كادوا.
The clause «أوحينا ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذي).
The clause «تفتري ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «اتّخذوك ...» has no grammatical position, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. if you had done that, they would have taken you as a close friend; and the condition clause has no grammatical position, conjoined to a resumptive clause.
74- (الواو) a conjunction (لولا) a conditional particle that does not put into the jussive (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle (ثبّتناك) like أوحينا.. and (الكاف) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (اللام) occurring in the apodosis of لولا (قد) a particle of expectation — or of diminution (taqlīl) — (كدت) a past defective verb.. and (التاء) is a pronoun in the position of a nominative, the noun of كاد (تركن) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "anta" (إليهم) like إليك, attached to (تركن), (شيئا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun), accusative (قليلا) naʿt (adjective) of (شيئا), accusative..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن ثبّتناك..) is in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar is necessarily omitted, its implied form being موجود ("existing").
The clause «لولا تثبيتنا أيّاك بالعصمة ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause كادوا.
The clause «ثبّتناك ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن).
The clause «كدت تركن ...» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «تركن ...» is in the position of an accusative, the khabar of كدت.
75- (إذا لأذقناك) like إذا لاتّخذوك (ضعف) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (الحياة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and in the speech there is the omission of a muḍāf, i.e.: double the punishment of life (الواو) a conjunction (ضعف الممات) like ضعف الحياة and conjoined to it (ثمّ) a conjunction (لا) negating (تجد) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "anta" (اللام) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to an omitted second object (على) a preposition and (نا) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (نصيرا), which is the first mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The clause «أذقناك ...» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: if you had done — or inclined — We would have made you taste..
The clause «لا تجد ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أذقناك.
76- (الواو) a conjunction (إن كادوا ليستفزّونك من الأرض) like إن كادوا ليفتنونك عن الذي.. (اللام) for giving the reason (يخرجوك) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the fāʿil, and (الكاف) is mafʿūl bihi (من) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (يخرجوك)..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يخرجوك..) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to (يستفزّونك).
(الواو) a conjunction (إذا) with tanwīn, like the first (لا) negating (يلبثون) like يفتنون (خلافك) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (يلبثون), and (الكاف) is muḍāf ilayhi (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr) (قليلا) standing in for the maṣdar, mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative [Note: or standing in for the adverb, i.e. except a little time.].
The clause «إن كادوا ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the first clause كادوا.
The clause «يستفزّونك ...» is in the position of an accusative, the khabar of كادوا.
The clause «يلبثون ...» has no grammatical position, the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. if they had expelled you, they would not remain ... and the implied condition clause has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause إن كادوا (the second).

* Morphology:
(خليلا): an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from خلّه, i.e. his sincere friend; the adjective has come from a non-triliteral anomalously (shudhūdhan); its pattern is فعيل.
(أذقناك): it contains a change by deletion (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf) suiting its being built on sukūn; its original form is أذاقناك, and when two quiescent letters met, the alif — the ʿayn of the verb — was dropped, because it is a hollow weak verb; its pattern is أفلناك.

* Rhetoric:
1- Exaggeration in diminishing the near-occurrence (al-kaydūda):
in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «وَإِنْ كادُوا لَيَفْتِنُونَكَ».
In this noble verse there is exaggeration in diminishing the near-occurrence, because the mere gentleness that policy and winning over the people required was held against the Prophet ﷺ, since a sin grows great in proportion to the one who commits it, according to what has come down: «the good deeds of the pious are the bad deeds of those brought near».
2- Ellipsis (al-ḥadhf):
in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «لَأَذَقْناكَ ضِعْفَ الْحَياةِ وَضِعْفَ الْمَماتِ».
The original form of the speech is: We would have made you taste a doubled punishment in life and a doubled punishment in death. Then the qualified noun was omitted and the adjective, which is "double", was put in its place. Then the adjective was annexed as the qualified noun would be annexed, so it was said: ضعف الحياة، وضعف الممات, as though it were said:
لأذقناك أليم الحياة وأليم الممات.

* Benefits:
1- The Messenger's stance towards Thaqīf.
History tells us that Thaqīf asked the Messenger ﷺ to single them out with things they could boast of over the Arabs; among them was their saying: that we not pay the tithe, nor be mustered, nor bow down in our prayer; that every usury owed to us is ours, and every usury owed by us is remitted from us; that you let us enjoy al-Lāt for a year, so that we may take what is offered to it, and when we have taken it we will break it and embrace Islam; and that you make our valley sacred as Mecca was made sacred; and if the Arabs say: why did you do that, then say: Allah commanded me to. They brought their document, and he wrote: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. This is a document from Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, to Thaqīf: they shall not be tithed and shall not be mustered. They said: nor bow down (ولا يحبّون) [Translator's note: so spelled in the source here and below; يجبّون, as in نجبّي above, is meant].
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was silent. Then they said to the scribe: write «لا يحبّون», and the scribe was looking at the Messenger of Allah. Then ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb stood up, drew his sword and said: You have inflamed the heart of our Prophet — O people of Thaqīf — may Allah inflame your hearts with fire! They said: we are not speaking to you, we are only speaking to Muhammad. That was the cause of the revelation of the verses mentioned.
Of course: لا نعشر means: a tenth of our wealth is not taken from us. ولا نحشر means: we are not driven out to jihad.
ولا نجبّي في صلاتنا means: they do not bow or prostrate.
In one narration, they asked to be exempted from prayer. The Messenger granted them the first two requests, but said: there is no good in a religion in which there is no bowing and prostrating — or as he said.
It is natural that these verses annulled the agreement that Thaqīf tried to dictate to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and defined the position of Islam towards them and those like them. Further, we must take up in the discussion the verb كاد, for it is repeated in these verses several times.
Ibn Hishām has an enjoyable discussion of this verb, in which he refutes some grammarians and parsers on some of what they became known for, including their saying: that «كاد» — its affirmation is negation and its negation is affirmation; so if it is said: كاد يفعل, its meaning is that he did not do it, and if it is said: لم يكد يفعل, its meaning is that he did it. al-Maʿmarī [Translator's note: so in the source, «المعمري»] went to the like of that in a discussion we can dispense with recounting, for fear of lengthiness. What is correct is that its ruling is the ruling of all other verbs: its negation is negation and its affirmation is affirmation, as is shown by its meaning being approximation; so «كاد يفعل» means he came near to doing it, and «ما كاد يفعل» means he did not come near to doing it. An example of that is «إذا أخرج يده لم يكد يراها». So reflect and consider — may Allah inspire you with right guidance..!

safi-cedvel:77-77.t:
* I'rab:
(سنّة) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, the implied sense being: سنّنا ذلك سنّة ("We made that a practice") [Note: It may be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being اتّبع ("follow").. al-Farrāʾ allowed its accusative to be by removal of the preposition, i.e.: like the practice of Allah regarding those We have sent, with the preposition attached to (يستفزّونك) or to (لا يلبثون) in the preceding [verse].], (من) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a genitive (majrūr), muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) (قد) a particle of verification (taḥqīq) (أرسلنا) a past verb and its fāʿil (agent) (قبلك) an adverb of time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أرسلنا), and (الكاف) is muḍāf ilayhi (من رسلنا) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the omitted object of أرسلنا, i.e. We sent him from among Our messengers (الواو) a conjunction (لا تجد.. تحويلا) like لا تجد.. نصيرا [Note: in verse (75) of this sūra.], (لسنّتنا) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi, and (نا) is muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قد أرسلنا ...» is a clause with no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «لا تجد ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the implied clause سنّنا.

safi-cedvel:78-81.t:
* I'rab:
(أقم) an imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "anta" (الصلاة) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) (لدلوك) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أقم) [Note: This lām means "after", i.e. after the declining of the sun, as in their saying كتبته لثلاث خلون ("I wrote it after three [nights] had passed"); and it may be for giving the reason, i.e. for the sake of the declining of the sun or because of the declining of the sun.], (الشمس) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) (إلى غسق) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أقم) [Note: It may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الصلاة, i.e. continuing..], (الليل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (الواو) a conjunction (قرآن) conjoined to الصلاة, accusative [Note: or it is a mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being أقم or الزم ("hold to"), and the conjoining is then a conjoining of clauses.], (الفجر) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (إنّ) a particle of emphasis and accusative (قرآن) the noun of إنّ, accusative (الفجر) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (كان) a past defective verb — an abrogator (nāsikh) — its noun being a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو" (مشهودا) the khabar (predicate) of كان, accusative.
The clause «أقم ...» is a clause with no grammatical position, resumptive.
The clause «إنّ قرآن الفجر ...» has no grammatical position, giving the reason (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «كان مشهودا» is in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ), the khabar of إنّ.
79- (الواو) a conjunction (من الليل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being اسهر من الليل ("stay awake part of the night") [Note: (من) here is either partitive, i.e. a part of the night, or in the sense of (في), i.e. stay awake in the night, or stand in the night.], (الفاء) a conjunction (تهجّد) like (أقم) (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (تهجّد), and the pronoun refers to the Qur'an [Note: i.e. pray the night vigil with the Qur'an, so التهجّد means prayer.. or the pronoun refers to the night, i.e. stay awake in the night.] (نافلة) ḥāl, accusative, of the omitted object, i.e. pray the night vigil in the state of its being supererogatory [Note: It may be a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun) because it has its meaning, i.e. perform it as a supererogatory act; and if التهجّد is explained as prayer, (نافلة) is a mafʿūl bihi.], (اللام) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (نافلة) (عسى) a complete (tāmm) past verb (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative particle (يبعثك) an imperfect verb, accusative.. and (الكاف) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (ربّك) fāʿil, nominative.. and (الكاف) is muḍāf ilayhi (مقاما) ḥāl, accusative, with an implied muḍāf, i.e. "possessing a station" [Note: It may be a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, i.e. you will stand a standing; and it may be an adverb attached to (يبعثك).], (محمودا) naʿt (adjective) of (مقاما), accusative..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يبعثك..) is in the position of a nominative, the fāʿil of عسى.
The clause «(اسهر) من الليل» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أقم..
The clause «تهجّد ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause (اسهر).
The clause «عسى أن يبعثك» has no grammatical position, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) — or giving the reason —.
The clause «يبعثك ربّك ...» has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).
80- (الواو) a conjunction (قل) like أقم (ربّ) the one addressed (munādā), annexed, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ that was dropped for lightening.. and the dropped (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi (أدخلني) an imperative verb, and (النون) is for protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and (الياء) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "anta", and the second object of أدخلني is omitted, its implied form being "Medina" (مدخل) mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative (صدق) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (الواو) a conjunction (أخرجني مخرج صدق) like its counterpart preceding it (الواو) a conjunction (اجعل) like أدخل (اللام) a preposition and (الياء) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (من لدنك) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the second object.. and (الكاف) is muḍāf ilayhi (سلطانا) first mafʿūl bihi, accusative (نصيرا) naʿt of (سلطانا), accusative.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تهجّد.
The clause of «the vocative and its answer ...» is in the position of an accusative, the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أدخلني ...» has no grammatical position, the answer to the vocative.
The clause «أخرجني ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أدخلني.
The clause «اجعل ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause أدخلني.
81- (الواو) a conjunction (قل) like the previous (جاء) a past verb (الحقّ) fāʿil, nominative (الواو) a conjunction (زهق الباطل) like جاء الحقّ (إنّ الباطل كان زهوقا) like إنّ قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause قل (the first).
The clause «جاء الحقّ ...» is in the position of an accusative, the object of the saying.
The clause «زهق الباطل ...» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause جاء الحقّ.
The clause «إنّ الباطل كان ...» has no grammatical position, giving the reason.
The clause «كان زهوقا» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of إنّ.

* Morphology:
(دلوك): the maṣdar of the verb دلكت الشمس دلوكا, of the نصر class, i.e. it passed the meridian or inclined towards setting; according to al-Zamakhsharī it is derived from الدلك ("rubbing"), because a person rubs his eyes when looking at the sun; its pattern is فعول with ḍamma on the fāʾ.
(غسق): the maṣdar of the triliteral verb غسق يغسق الليل, of the ضرب class, i.e. its darkness intensified; its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas.
(نافلة): a noun for the prayer in addition to the obligatory one, on the pattern فاعلة.
(مقاما): it may be meant as the mīm-maṣdar (maṣdar mīmī) of the triliteral قام, and it may be meant as the noun of place.. see verse (125) of al-Baqara.
(محمودا): a passive participle from the triliteral حمد, on the pattern مفعول.
(مدخل): a mīm-maṣdar from the quadriliteral أدخل; its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn.
(مخرج): a mīm-maṣdar from the quadriliteral أخرج; its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn.
(زهوقا): an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) from the triliteral زهق يزهق, of the فتح class, meaning "it dwindled and vanished"; it may be an intensive form of the active participle; its pattern is فعول with fatḥa on the fāʾ.

* Rhetoric:
1- The loose figure (al-majāz al-mursal):
in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ».
The part is used for the whole, i.e. the recitation of dawn, and what is meant by it is the prayer, because recitation is part of it; so the relation is partiality (juzʾiyya).
2- Using the overt noun where a pronoun was expected (al-iẓhār fī maqām al-iḍmār):
in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كانَ مَشْهُوداً» after His saying: «وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ».
The overt noun occurs where a pronoun was expected, and He, glory be to Him, did not say إنه, for greater emphasis and attention.
3- The subtle antithesis (al-muqābala al-laṭīfa):
in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «أَدْخِلْنِي مُدْخَلَ صِدْقٍ» and «أَخْرِجْنِي مُخْرَجَ صِدْقٍ», and between «جاءَ الْحَقُّ» and «وَزَهَقَ الْباطِلُ».
4- On the tail-clause (al-tadhyīl):
in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «وَقُلْ جاءَ الْحَقُّ وَزَهَقَ الْباطِلُ إِنَّ الْباطِلَ كانَ زَهُوقاً».
This device is: that the poet or prose writer appends to his speech, after it is complete and it is fine to stop on it, a clause that verifies the speech before it, adds emphasis to it, and runs in it like a proverb, for greater verification.
This verse is among the greatest examples of it: the last clause is the tadhyīl that came out in the form of a current proverb.

* Benefits:
1- The noun of place and the noun of time.
1- They are two nouns formed for the time of the occurrence of the action or its place:
2- They are formed from the triliteral whose imperfect has ḍamma or fatḥa on the ʿayn on the pattern «مفعل» [Translator's note: i.e. with fatḥa on the ʿayn], and likewise when the verb is weak in the lām, as in مرمى and مسعى.
3- They are formed from the triliteral, when it has kasra on the ʿayn, or is assimilated (mithāl), on the pattern «مفعل» [Translator's note: i.e. with kasra on the ʿayn], as in مجلس, موعد and ميسر.
4- Excepted from those with ḍamma on the ʿayn are eleven words that came with kasra, namely:
منسك ومطلع ومشرق ومغرب ومرفق ومفرق ومجزر ومنبت ومسقط ومسكن ومسجد.
5- They are formed from the non-triliteral on the pattern of the passive participle, such as: مدخل ومخرج ومنطلق ومستودع, as we have observed in the verse under discussion.
Remark: so the form of time, place, the mīm-maṣdar and the passive participle from the non-triliteral is on a single pattern, and likewise in some triliteral patterns; they are distinguished by context (qarīna).
6- A noun of place is frequently formed from the non-derived (jāmid) noun on «مفعلة», to indicate the abundance of a thing in a place, as in «مأسدة», «مسبعة» and «مقثأة», for the spot where lions, beasts of prey or cucumbers abound. Despite its frequent occurrence it is not regular (qiyāsī); rather most of it is aurally transmitted (samāʿī).
Remark: as we have seen, a tāʾ marbūṭa may attach to the nouns of time and place, as in مقبرة, مطبعة and مدرسة. All of that is aurally transmitted, not a basis for analogy.
2- If we open Mughnī al-Labīb we find that the genitive-governing «اللام» has twenty-two meanings; we mention them to you without illustration, to avoid lengthiness:
ownership, quasi-ownership, transitivization (taʿdiya), giving the reason, emphasis — which is the intrusive and inserted one — and the lām of the one whose help is sought (al-mustaghāth); then strengthening the governor, and agreement with إلى; the lām of oath, the lām of wonder, the lām of outcome (ṣayrūra) and transitivization, superiority (istiʿlāʾ), agreement with في, agreement with عند, agreement with من, the lām of conveying (tablīgh), agreement with عن, conferring ownership (tamlīk), giving the reason, the one entering the imperfect, the lām of emphasizing negation, and the lām of clarification (tabyīn), which is of three kinds: for clarifying the object, clarifying agency that is confused between two objects, and the reverse.

safi-cedvel:1-1.t:
* I'rab:
(سبحان) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, accusative (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (أسرى) a past verb, indeclinable on the implied fatḥa on the alif, and the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هو" (he), and it is the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) (بعبده) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أسرى), and (الهاء) is an attached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (ليلا) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (أسرى) (من المسجد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أسرى) (الحرام) naʿt of مسجد, genitive (إلى المسجد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أسرى) (الأقصى) naʿt of the second المسجد, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the implied kasra on the alif (الذي) a relative, in the position of the genitive, a second naʿt of المسجد (باركنا) a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn.. and (نا) is an attached pronoun in the position of the nominative, agent (حوله) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (باركنا), and (الهاء) is like the first (اللام) for giving a reason (نريه) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām.. and (الهاء) is an attached pronoun in the position of the accusative, mafʿūl bihi, and the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "نحن" (We), for magnification.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن نريه) is in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (أسرى).
(من آياتنا) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (نريه).. and (نا) is an attached pronoun in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (إنّ) a particle of emphasis and accusative, and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of the accusative, the noun of inna (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ [Note: or in the position of the accusative — it being borrowed for that — as tawkīd (emphasis) of the attached pronoun of the third person, the noun of inna.] (السميع) khabar, nominative (البصير) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause « (يسبّح) سبحان ... » has no grammatical position; it is an inceptive clause (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «أسرى ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (الذي).
The clause «باركنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second relative noun (الذي).
The clause «نريه ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-type relative (أن).
The clause «إنّه هو السميع ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «هو السميع ... » is in the position of the nominative, as khabar of inna.

* Morphology:
(أسرى): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by substitution; its origin is أسري with a yāʾ; the yāʾ had a vowel after a fatḥa and was turned into an alif.
(الأقصى): in form an elative (ism tafḍīl) on the pattern أفعل, then the sense of description, not of comparison, was intended by it. It contains iʿlāl by substitution: its origin is الأقصى with a yāʾ at its end, and when what precedes the yāʾ came to have a fatḥa the yāʾ was turned into an alif.. and the lām of the word is a wāw or a yāʾ, because its verb is قصا يقصو, قصي يقصى, and its meaning is "to be far".

* Rhetoric:
«سُبْحانَ الَّذِي أَسْرى بِعَبْدِهِ لَيْلًا» 1- Mention (al-dhikr): the isrāʾ (night journey) can only occur at night, so what is the meaning of mentioning the night?
The apparent point is that the purpose of mentioning the night, even though أسرى already conveys it, is to depict the journey in its form in the mind of the hearer: as if أسرى indicated two matters, one of them the travelling, the other its being at night, and it was desired to single out one of them for mention, to fix it in the mind of the addressee and to alert him that it is intended by the mention.
A parallel for singling out one of what the preceding expression indicates, together with another, is His saying, the Exalted:
«وَقالَ اللَّهُ لا تَتَّخِذُوا إِلهَيْنِ اثْنَيْنِ إِنَّما هُوَ إِلهٌ واحِدٌ». The noun that bears the dual indicates the dual and the genus, and so too the singular; so alerting was intended, because one of the two meanings, namely the dual, is intended and meant; and likewise awakening was intended, because oneness is the aim in His saying:
(إِنَّما هُوَ إِلهٌ واحِدٌ). Had it been confined to «إنما هو إله», it would have suggested that the important matter was to establish divinity for Him, whereas the aim of the speech is only to establish oneness.
2- Indefiniteness (al-tankīr): in His saying «ليلا».
By «ليلا», in indefinite form, He intended to make the duration of the journey short, and that He made him journey in part of the night from Mecca to Syria, a journey of forty nights; for the indefiniteness here indicates something of the sense of partiality. The reading of ʿAbdallāh and Ḥudhayfa bears witness to this: «من الليل», i.e. "part of the night".
3- Iltifāt (shift of person): in His saying, the Exalted «الَّذِي بارَكْنا حَوْلَهُ لِنُرِيَهُ مِنْ آياتِنا- إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ» the speech is turned from the third person in His saying, the Exalted «سُبْحانَ الَّذِي أَسْرى بِعَبْدِهِ» to the form of the magnifying first person in «باركنا- ونريه- آياتنا», to magnify the blessings and the signs; for just as it indicates the magnification of what the pronoun refers to, so it indicates the greatness of what is annexed to it and issues from it, as it is said: "only the great does the great". They have mentioned a particular point about this variation: that His saying, the Exalted «الَّذِي أَسْرى بِعَبْدِهِ لَيْلًا» indicates his journey, upon him be blessings and peace, from the world of witnessing to the world of the unseen, so the third person is the more fitting for it. His saying, the Exalted «بارَكْنا حَوْلَهُ» indicates the sending down of blessings, which suits the magnification of the One who sends down, and the expression by the pronoun of majesty ensures that. His saying, Glorified is He, «لنريه» is in the sense of distance of connection and rarity of presence, so the speaker in direct address suits it. His saying, the Exalted «مِنْ آياتِنا»
is a return to magnification, as the indication has preceded. As for the third person in His saying, Mighty and Majestic, «إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ», on the assumption that the pronoun refers to Him, the Exalted — which is the more apparent and the view of most — it is so as to agree with His saying «بعبده»; and this is strengthened by the specification, which places this iltifāt in the best of places and fits the giving of reason most fully, since the meaning is: He brought him near and singled him out with this honour because He, Glorified, is aware of his states, knowing his worthiness of this station.

* Benefits:
- The grammarians agree that the principal meaning of the preposition (من) is ibtidāʾ al-ghāya (the beginning of the limit).
A question arises: is it for the beginning of the limit in both time and place?
The answer is that the grammarians agree that it is for the beginning of the limit in place, and differ about its being for the beginning of the limit in time.
The Kufans and some of the Basrans hold that it is, and that is the sound view; it has occurred in the Noble Book and in the noble Ḥadīth, and there is no proof beyond that:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said «مطرنا من الجمعة إلى الجمعة» ("It rained on us from Friday to Friday").
Al-Nābigha al-Dhubyānī says:
تخيّرون من أزمان يوم حلية ... إلى اليوم قد جربن كل التجارب
(Gloss: "they have been chosen from the times of the day of Ḥilya to this day; they have tried every trial." [Translator's note: the source reads حلية; the usual form of the verse has حليمة.])
As for the preposition «إلى», the grammarians agree that it conveys the end of the limit, whether in time or place. An example of the temporal is His saying, the Exalted: «ثُمَّ أَتِمُّوا الصِّيامَ إِلَى اللَّيْلِ» and an example of the spatial is His saying, the Exalted: «إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ الْأَقْصَى». Whoever wishes to exhaust the meanings of the two particles should consult the longer works, for in them is quenching for every thirsty one.

safi-cedvel:2-6.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction — or resumptive (آتينا) like باركنا [Note: in verse (1) of the sūra], (موسى) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the implied fatḥa — and it is prevented from tanwīn because it is a proper name and foreign (الكتاب) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (الواو) a conjunction (جعلناه) like باركنا.. and (الهاء) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (هدى) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative [Note: and if the verb is given the sense of "We made him" then (هدى) is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl.], the sign of the accusative being the implied fatḥa on the alif (لبني) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (هدى) [Note: or attached to (جعلناه)], the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ, for it is appended to the sound masculine plural (إسرائيل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa, because it is a proper name and foreign [Translator's note: i.e. a diptote] (أن) a particle of explanation [Note: what precedes it has the sense of saying without its letters, namely the word الكتاب, i.e. "We said in it: do not take…". It is also permissible that (أن) be a maṣdar particle that governs the accusative.], (لا) prohibitive [Note: or redundant if (أن) is a maṣdar particle, and the implied form then is: "We made it a guidance… lest you take…"; the interpreted maṣdar is then a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) with an omitted muḍāf.], (تتّخذوا) an imperfect verb, jussive, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. [Note: or accusative by أن, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the agent] and (الواو) is the agent (من دوني) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a second mafʿūl whose governor is تتّخذوا [Note: or it is attached to (تتّخذوا), the first mafʿūl being (ذرّيّة) and the second (وكيلا).. and it is permissible that the adverbial be attached to a ḥāl from (وكيلا)] and (الياء) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (وكيلا) the first mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The clause «آتينا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the inceptive [Note: or it is resumptive, with no grammatical position.].
The clause «جعلناه ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause آتينا..
The clause «تتّخذوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is explicative.
3- (ذرّية) badal of (وكيلا), accusative [Note: concerning the accusative of (ذريّة) the exegetes have different views, among them: it is the first mafʿūl bihi of the verb تتّخذوا — as in note no. (1) — and the second mafʿūl is (وكيلا), i.e.: "do not take the offspring of those We carried with Noah as guardians". Among them: that it is a badal of (وكيلا) — as in the i'rab above. Or it is accusative as the object of specification (ikhtiṣāṣ), the view of al-Zamakhsharī; or it is a vocative, the view of al-Suyūṭī.
(4, 5, 6) in verse (1) of the sūra], (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (حملنا) like (باركنا) «4» (مع) an adverb, accusative, attached to (حملنا) (إنّه) like the preceding «5» (كان) an incomplete past verb (a governing verb), and its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he" (عبدا) khabar of كان (شكورا) naʿt of (عبدا), accusative.
The clause «حملنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «إنّه كان ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
The clause «كان عبدا ... » is in the position of the nominative, as khabar of inna.
4- (الواو) a conjunction (قضينا) like باركنا «6», (إلى بني إسرائيل) like لبني إسرائيل [Note: in verse (2) of the sūra], attached to (قضينا) by its being given the sense of "We revealed" or "We carried out" (في الكتاب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (قضينا) (اللام) the lām of the oath, for an implied oath (تفسدنّ) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the persistence of the nūn, which has been dropped because of the succession of similar letters, and the omitted (الواو), dropped because of the meeting of two sākin letters, is the agent, and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis (في الأرض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تفسدنّ) (مرّتين) mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, whose governor is تفسدنّ, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ (الواو) a conjunction (لتعلنّ) like (لتفسدنّ) and conjoined to it (علوّا) mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative (كبيرا) naʿt of (علوا), accusative.
The clause «قضينا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause آتينا.
The clause «تفسدنّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to an implied oath [Note: or the response of an oath for His saying: وقضينا.. because it is given the sense of an oath; hence their saying قضى الله لأفعلنّ ("Allah decreed: I shall surely do…"), they treat decree and destiny as an oath.].
The clause «تعلنّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause تفسدنّ [Note: or it is the response of an implied oath conjoined to the first oath].
5- (الفاء) a conjunction (إذا) an adverb of future time, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, attached to (بعثنا) (جاء) a past verb (وعد) agent, nominative (أولاهما) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the implied kasra on the alif.. and (هما) is an attached pronoun in the position of the genitive, muḍāf ilayhi (بعثنا) like باركنا [Note: in verse (1) of this sūra], (على) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (بعثنا) (عبادا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (اللام) a preposition and (نا) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to a naʿt of (عبادا) (أولي) a second naʿt, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ, for it is appended to the sound masculine plural (بأس) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (شديد) naʿt of بأس, genitive (الفاء) a conjunction (جاسوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and (الواو) is the agent (خلال) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (جاسوا) (الديار) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (الواو) parenthetical — or circumstantial (كان) an incomplete past verb (a governing verb), and its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "it", i.e. the ravaging or the promise mentioned (وعدا) khabar of كان, accusative (مفعولا) naʿt of (وعدا), accusative.
The clause «جاء وعد ... » is in the position of the genitive, as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «بعثنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «جاسوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause بعثنا.
The clause «كان وعدا ... » has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical [Note: or in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, with an implied قد
(2, 3, 4) or attached to the maṣdar (الكرّة.. or to a ḥāl from it).].
6- (ثمّ) a conjunction (رددنا) like باركنا «2», (لكم) like عليكم, attached to (رددنا) (الكرّة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (عليهم) like عليكم, attached to (رددنا) «3» (الواو) a conjunction (أمددناكم) like باركنا «4», and (كم) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (بأموال) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أمددناكم) (بنين) conjoined to أموال by the wāw and genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ, for it is appended to the sound masculine plural (الواو) a conjunction (وجعلناكم) like أمددناكم (أكثر) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (نفيرا) tamyīz (specification), accusative.
The clause «رددنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause بعثنا.
The clause «أمددناكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause بعثنا.
The clause «جعلناكم ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause بعثنا.

* Morphology:
(تعلنّ): the wāw of the group was dropped because of the meeting of two sākin letters with the first nūn of the doubled nūn of emphasis.. It contains iʿlāl by omission; its origin is تعلوونّ: the weak letter, the lām of the word, met the wāw of the group, and the weak letter was dropped because both are sākin.. then the omission proceeds as it does in sound verbs attached to the wāw of the group and the yāʾ of the feminine addressee when they are emphasised with the nūn of emphasis.. Its pattern is تفعنّ, with a fatḥa on the tāʾ and a ḍamma on the ʿayn.
(علوّا): a maṣdar of علا يعلو, and it is samāʿī (by usage), on the pattern فعلّ with two ḍammas.
(الكرّة): originally a maṣdar of the triliteral verb كرّ, on the pattern فعلة with fatḥa then sukūn, and it is sometimes used to express victory.
(نفيرا): it is فعيل in the sense of فاعل, or the plural of نفر like عبد and عبيد, or it is a maṣdar meaning going out on an expedition.

safi-cedvel:7-7.t:
* I'rab:
(إن) a conditional particle that jussively governs (أحسنتم) a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of the jussive, being the protasis.. and (تم) is the pronoun of the agent (أحسنتم) like the first, the apodosis (لأنفسكم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the second (أحسنتم)..
and (كم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) a conjunction (إن أسأتم) like إن أحسنتم (الفاء) linking the apodosis (اللام) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: "your doing evil" (الفاء) a conjunction (إذا جاء وعد الآخرة) like إذا جاء وعد أولاهما [Note: in verse (5) of this sūra], i.e. the last time (اللام) for giving a reason (يسوءوا) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn ... and (الواو) is the agent (وجوهكم) mafʿūl bihi, accusative.. and (كم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) a conjunction (ليدخلوا المسجد) like ليسوءوا وجوهكم (الكاف) a preposition, of comparison (ما) a maṣdar particle (دخلوه) a past verb and its agent, and (الهاء) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (أوّل) mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar [Note: or it is a mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial) standing in for the adverb, accusative.] accusative (مرّة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.

* Morphology:
(علوا): it contains iʿlāl by omission because of the meeting of two sākin letters: the lām of the verb and the wāw of the group met, both sākin, so the lām of the verb, the weak letter alif, was dropped, and what precedes the wāw stayed with a fatḥa as an indication of it. (تتبيرا): a regular maṣdar of the verb يتبّروا, on the pattern تفعيل.

(حصيرا): a derived adjective; it is فعيل in the sense of فاعل, i.e. "encompassing"; and (حصيرا) may also be in the sense of a mat that is spread for them, and it is then rigid.

safi-cedvel:9-10.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ) a particle resembling the verb (ها) a particle of alerting (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, the noun of inna (القرآن) badal of ذا — or ʿaṭf bayān — accusative (يهدي) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the yāʾ, and the agent is "he" [Note: and its object is omitted, i.e. "guides all people…"], (اللام) a preposition (التي) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to (يهدي), (هي) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ (أقوم) khabar, nominative (الواو) a conjunction (يبشّر) like يهدي (المؤمنين) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, naʿt of المؤمنين (يعملون) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the persistence of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the agent (الصالحات) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra (أنّ) a particle of emphasis and accusative (اللام) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to the khabar of أنّ (أجرا) the noun of أنّ, accusative (كبيرا) naʿt of (أجرا), accusative.

safi-cedvel:11-11.t:
* I'rab:

The clause «كان الإنسان عجولا ... » has no grammatical position; it is a resumption with the sense of giving a reason.

* Morphology:
(يدع): it was written in the muṣḥaf without the wāw, contrary to the analogy of the orthography, since the verb is nominative; but when it dropped out in recitation because of the meeting of two sākin letters, it dropped out in writing contrary to analogy, and a parallel is سندع الزبانية [Note: in Sūra al-ʿAlaq, verse (18)].
(عجولا): an assimilated adjective (ṣifa mushabbaha) — or a form of intensification — from عجل يعجل of the intransitive bāb of فرح; its pattern is فعول, with a fatḥa on the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:12-14.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (جعلنا) a past verb.. and (نا) is the pronoun of the agent (الليل) the first mafʿūl bihi (النهار) conjoined to الليل by the wāw, accusative (آيتين) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ (الفاء) a conjunction (محونا) like جعلنا, (آية) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (الليل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (الواو) a conjunction (جعلنا آية النهار) like محونا آية الليل (مبصرة) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (اللام) of causation (تبتغوا) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the agent (فضلا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (من ربّكم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تبتغوا) [Note: or attached to a naʿt of (فضلا)].. and (كم) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) a conjunction (لتعلموا عدد) like لتبتغوا فضلا (السنين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ, for it is appended to the sound masculine plural, (الواو) a conjunction (الحساب) conjoined to عدد, accusative.

The clause «جعلنا (the second) ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause محونا.

The clause «تعلموا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the second (أن).
The clause « (فصّلنا) كلّ شيء ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive.
