The clause « (ألزمنا) كلّ إنسان ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive.
The clause «ألزمناه ... » has no grammatical position; it is explicative.
The clause «نخرج ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause ألزمنا كلّ..
The clause «يلقاه ... » is in the position of the accusative, as naʿt of (كتابا).
14- (اقرأ) an imperative verb, and the agent is "you" (كتابك) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (الكاف) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (كفى) a past verb, indeclinable on the implied fatḥa (الباء) a redundant preposition (نفسك) genitive in form, nominative in position, agent of كفى, and (الكاف) is like the first (اليوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (كفى) (على) a preposition and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (حسيبا), which is a tamyīz [Note: or an accusative ḥāl; the word is masculine because it is in the position of the witness, the judge and the trustee; so حسيب is in the sense of حاسب ("reckoner"), and it is permissible to interpret النفس as meaning the person], accusative.
The clause «اقرأ ... » is in the position of the accusative, as the reported speech of an implied saying which is a ḥāl from the agent of نخرج, i.e. "saying: read…".
The clause «كفى بنفسك ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.

* Morphology:
(طائره): the ṭāʾir is well known; its form is فاعل from طار; here it comes in the sense of deed, or the book of deeds, by istiʿāra (metaphor); or it is a kināya (allusion) for what Allah has decreed, which clings to a person and reaches him without deviating from him.
(عنقه): a rigid noun for the well-known organ; its pattern is فعل with two ḍammas.
(منشورا): a passive participle of the triliteral verb نشر; its pattern is مفعول.

* Rhetoric:
1- Majāz (figurative usage): in His saying, the Exalted «وَجَعَلْنا آيَةَ النَّهارِ مُبْصِرَةً».
It is majāz by the relation of causation, or the attribution is figurative, as in "his day is fasting"; the meaning is that its people see; and the attribution to the day is also figurative, being attribution to the customary cause, the real agent being Allah the Exalted.
2- Istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya (explicit metaphor): in His saying, the Exalted: «وَكُلَّ إِنسانٍ أَلْزَمْناهُ طائِرَهُ فِي عُنُقِهِ».
They used to take omens from birds and called it zajr; when they travelled and a bird passed them they would scare it off. If it passed them sāniḥan, passing from the left side to the right, they took it as a good omen; and if it passed bāriḥan, passing from the right side to the left, they took it as an evil omen. Hence it was called taṭayyur. When they ascribed good and evil to the bird, the word was borrowed, by explicit metaphor, for what resembles it of Allah's decree, the Exalted, and the deed of the servant, because it is a cause of good and evil. From this comes the saying "the ṭāʾir of Allah, the Exalted, not your ṭāʾir", i.e. the prevailing decree of Allah, mighty is His station, to which good and evil are ascribed, not your ṭāʾir by which you take ill omen or good omen.

safi-cedvel:15-16.t:
* I'rab:
(من) a conditional noun that jussively governs, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ (اهتدى) a past verb, indeclinable on the implied fatḥa on the alif, in the position of the jussive, being the protasis, and the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he" (الفاء) linking the apodosis (إنّما) kāffa and makfūfa (يهتدي) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the yāʾ, and the agent is "he" (لنفسه) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl from the agent of يهتدي, and (الهاء) is muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) a conjunction (من ضلّ فإنّما يضلّ) like من اهتدى.. (على) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to a ḥāl from the agent of يضلّ (الواو) a conjunction (لا) negative (تزر) an imperfect verb, nominative (وازرة) agent, nominative, and it is a naʿt of an omitted described noun, i.e. "a soul that bears" (وزر) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (أخرى) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the implied kasra on the alif, and it is a naʿt of an omitted described noun, i.e. "another soul" (الواو) a conjunction (ما) for negation (كنّا) an incomplete past verb (a governing verb) and (نا) is the noun of كان (معذّبين) khabar of كان, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ (حتّى) a particle of limit and of the genitive (نبعث) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after حتّى, and the agent is for magnification (رسولا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The clause «من اهتدى ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «اهتدى ... » is in the position of the nominative, as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) «1».
The clause «يهتدي ... » is in the position of the jussive, as the apodosis accompanied by the fāʾ «2».
The clause «من ضلّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause من اهتدى.
The clause «ضلّ.....» is in the position of the nominative, as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) «3».
The clause «يضلّ ... » is in the position of the jussive, as the apodosis accompanied by the fāʾ «4».
The clause «لا تزر وازرة ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive.
The clause «ما كنّا معذّبين ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to a clause with no position.
16- (الواو) a conjunction (إذا) an adverb of future time containing the sense of a condition, in the position of the accusative, attached to (أمرنا) (أردنا) a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn.. and (نا) is the agent (أن) a maṣdar particle that governs the accusative (نهلك) an imperfect verb, accusative, and the agent is "We", for magnification, (قرية) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (أمرنا) like أردنا (مترفيها) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.. and (ها) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (الفاء) a conjunction (فسقوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and (الواو) is the agent (في) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (فسقوا) (الفاء) a conjunction (حقّ) a past verb (عليها) like فيها, attached to (حقّ) (القول) agent, nominative (الفاء) a conjunction (دمّرناها) like أردنا.. and (ها) is mafʿūl bihi (تدميرا) mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن نهلك..) is in the position of the accusative, as mafʿūl bihi, whose governor is أردنا.
The clause «أردنا ... » is in the position of the genitive, as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «نهلك ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
The clause «أمرنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «فسقوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the apodosis clause.
The clause «حقّ عليها القول» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause فسقوا.
The clause «دمّرناها ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause حقّ عليها القول.

* Morphology:
(مترفيها): plural of مترف, a passive participle of the quadriliteral أترف; its pattern is مفعل, with a ḍamma on the mīm and a fatḥa on the ʿayn.
(تدميرا): a regular maṣdar of the quadriliteral verb دمّر; its pattern is تفعيل.

* Rhetoric:
1- Ṭibāq (antithesis): in His saying, the Exalted: «مَنِ اهْتَدى - وَمَنْ ضَلَّ» ..
Ṭibāq occurs in the verse between guidance (al-hudā) and error (al-ḍalāl).
2- Iltizām, or luzūm mā lā yalzam (the obligation of what is not obligatory):
in His saying, the Exalted: «أَمَرْنا مُتْرَفِيها فَفَسَقُوا فِيها».
Iltizām is the observing of one letter or two or more before the rawī (the rhyme letter), as far as the poet's or writer's capacity allows, without strain.
Here in «مترفيها» and «فيها» the fāʾ is observed before the yāʾ of the ridf (supporting letter), and the yāʾ is kept; much of it will come in the Noble Qur'an, and it is among the most elegant of usages.
3- Majāz (figurative usage): in His saying, the Exalted «أَمَرْنا مُتْرَفِيها».
The original is "We commanded its affluent to dissipate, so they dissipated", but intending the literal sense is impossible, so it is taken as majāz, either by the way of istiʿāra tamthīliyya (representational metaphor), by likening their state, in their plunging into blessings together with their disobedience and arrogance, to the state of one who has been commanded to do so; or by the way of istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya tabaʿiyya (explicit derivative metaphor), by likening the pouring out upon them of the blessings that make them arrogant to their being commanded to dissipate, the common ground being the driving to it and the causing of it.
4- Ḥadhf (omission): in His saying, the Exalted: «أَمَرْنا مُتْرَفِيها فَفَسَقُوا فِيها».
The thing commanded is omitted, and He did not say what He commanded them, for brevity of speech and in reliance on the hearer's intuition, because His saying «ففسقوا» indicates it, and it is widespread speech. It is said:
"I commanded him and he stood", "I commanded him and he recited"; nothing is understood from it except that what was commanded was standing or reciting, and were you to go about supposing something else, you would have sought from your addressee knowledge of the unseen.

* Benefits:
Ishtighāl (preoccupation):
It is a noun that precedes a governor that would by right put it in the accusative, were it not that the governor is occupied with acting upon the noun's pronoun, as in خالد أكرمه ("Khālid, I honoured him"). The preferred view is that the preceding noun is nominative as a mubtadaʾ and the clause after it is in the position of the nominative as its khabar.
There are people who have allowed its being accusative.
There is a long discussion about its being accusative or nominative that we have passed over for the sake of brevity.

safi-cedvel:17-17.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (كم) khabariyya (declarative), a substitute for a number, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, a fronted mafʿūl bihi (أهلكنا) a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn.. and (نا) is the agent (من القرون) tamyīz of كم (من بعد) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أهلكنا) (نوح) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (الواو) resumptive (كفى بربّك.. خبيرا) like كفى بنفسك حسيبا [Note: in verse (14) of this sūra], (بذنوب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (خبيرا أو بصيرا) ("Aware or Seeing"), (عباده) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (الهاء) is muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «أهلكنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «كفى بربّك ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

safi-cedvel:18-20.t:
* I'rab:
(من) like the preceding [Note: in verse (15) of this sūra.], (كان) an incomplete past verb, in the position of the jussive, being the protasis, and its noun is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he" (يريد) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the agent is "he" (العاجلة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (عجّلنا) like أهلكنا [Note: in the preceding verse (17).. and the verb is in the position of the jussive, being the apodosis.], (اللام) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (عجّلنا), (في) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (عجّلنا), (ما) a relative noun in the position of the accusative, mafʿūl bihi (نشاء) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the agent is "We", for magnification (اللام) a preposition (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the genitive, attached to (عجّلنا); it is a badal of (له), with the preposition repeated (نريد) like نشاء (ثمّ) a conjunction (جعلنا له) like عجّلنا له, and the preposition is attached to an omitted second mafʿūl (جهنّم) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; it is prevented from tanwīn because it is a proper name and feminine (يصلاها) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the alif..
and (ها) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the agent is "he" (مذموما) ḥāl from the agent, accusative (مدحورا) a second ḥāl, accusative.
The clause «من كان ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «كان يريد ... » is in the position of the nominative, as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: it is permissible that the khabar be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together.].
The clause «يريد ... » is in the position of the accusative, as khabar of كان.
The clause «عجّلنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis, not accompanied by the fāʾ.
The clause «نشاء ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «نريد ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (من).
The clause «جعلنا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause عجّلنا..
The clause «يصلاها ... » is in the position of the accusative, as a ḥāl from the pronoun in (له), or from جهنّم.
19- (الواو) a conjunction (من أراد) like من كان, and the agent is "he" (الآخرة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (الواو) a conjunction (سعى) a past verb, indeclinable on the implied fatḥa on the alif, in the position of the jussive, conjoined to أراد, and the agent is "he" (لها) like له, attached to (سعى) (سعيها) mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative [Note: or a mafʿūl bihi by giving سعى the sense of أعطى ("gave"), and سعيها means its work.], and (الهاء) is muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) the wāw of ḥāl (هو) a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ (مؤمن) khabar, nominative (الفاء) linking the apodosis (أولئك) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of the nominative, mubtadaʾ..
and (الكاف) is for address (كان) an incomplete past verb (سعيهم) the noun of كان, nominative..
and (هم) is muḍāf ilayhi (مشكورا) khabar of كان, accusative.
The clause «من أراد ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause من كان..
The clause «أراد الآخرة ... » is in the position of the nominative, as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: it is permissible that the khabar be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together.].
The clause «سعى لها ... » is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the clause أراد.
The clause «هو مؤمن ... » is in the position of the accusative, as a ḥāl from the agent of سعى.
The clause «أولئك كان سعيهم ... » is in the position of the jussive, as the apodosis accompanied by the fāʾ.
The clause «كان سعيهم مشكورا» is in the position of the nominative, as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).
20- (كلّا) a fronted mafʿūl bihi, accusative (نمدّ) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the agent is "We", for magnification (ها) a particle of alerting (أولاء) a demonstrative, a badal of (كلا), in the position of the accusative (الواو) a conjunction (هؤلاء) like the first and conjoined to it (من عطاء) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (نمدّ) (ربك) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.. and (الكاف) is muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) the wāw of ḥāl [Note: or resumptive, and the clause after it has no position, being resumptive.] (ما) negative (كان عطاء ربّك محظورا) like كان سعيهم مشكورا.
The clause «نمدّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
The clause «ما كان عطاء ربّك ... » is in the position of the accusative, as a ḥāl.

* Morphology:
(العاجلة): feminine of العاجل, an active participle of عجل on the pattern فاعل; here the adjective is used as a noun, and its meaning is this world.
(مذموما): a passive participle of the triliteral verb ذمّ; its pattern is مفعول.
(مشكورا): a passive participle of the triliteral verb شكر; its pattern is مفعول.
(محظورا): a passive participle of the triliteral verb حظر; its pattern is مفعول.

* Rhetoric:
- Laff and nashr (folding and unfolding): in His saying, the Exalted: «كُلًّا نُمِدُّ هؤُلاءِ وَهَؤُلاءِ».
It is an ordered laff and nashr: the first «هؤلاء» is the first group, i.e. the one who desires this world, and the second «هؤلاء» is for the second group, i.e. the one who desires the Hereafter.

safi-cedvel:21-21.t:
* I'rab:
(انظر) an imperative verb, and the agent is "you" (كيف) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, a ḥāl whose governor is (فضّلنا), which is a past verb and its agent (بعضهم) mafʿūl bihi, accusative.. and (هم) is muḍāf ilayhi (على بعض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (فضّلنا) (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya) (اللام) the lām of commencement (lām al-ibtidāʾ) (الآخرة) mubtadaʾ, nominative (أكبر) khabar, nominative (درجات) tamyīz, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra (الواو) a conjunction (أكبر تفضيلا) like أكبر درجات.
The clause «انظر ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «فضّلنا ... » is in the position of the accusative, as mafʿūl bihi, whose governor is the verb of looking, suspended by the interrogative كيف, and its meaning is "reflect"; and the clause is bound by the omitted preposition.
The clause «الآخرة أكبر ... » is in the position of the accusative, as a ḥāl [Note: it is permissible that it be resumptive, with no position.].

* Morphology:
(تفضيلا) a regular maṣdar of the quadriliteral verb فضّل; its pattern is تفعيل.

* Rhetoric:
- We spoke earlier about «luzūm mā lā yalzam» ("the obligation of what is not obligatory"), which is the observing of one letter, two letters or more before the rawī (rhyme letter) in poetry, and a parallel may occur in prose, such as His saying, the Exalted: «وَإِذا أَرَدْنا أَنْ نُهْلِكَ قَرْيَةً أَمَرْنا مُتْرَفِيها فَفَسَقُوا فِيها»
. In the Luzūmiyyāt of al-Maʿarrī there is a great deal of this art, such as his saying:
رويدك قد غررت وأنت حر ... بصاحب حيلة يعظ النساء

يحرم فيكم الصهباء صبحا ... ويشربها على عمد مساء

يقول لقد غدوت بلا كساء ... وفي لذاتها رهن الكساء
(Gloss: "Gently — you have been deceived, free man, by a crafty fellow who preaches to women; in the morning he forbids wine among you, and in the evening he drinks it deliberately; he says: 'I have gone out without a garment', while in its pleasures lies the pledge of the garment.")
And beware of this art, for going too far in it leads to hateful artificiality and rejected affectation.

safi-cedvel:22-22.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) a prohibitive that governs the jussive (تجعل) an imperfect verb, jussive, and the agent is "you" (مع) an adverb, accusative, attached to an omitted second mafʿūl (الله) the sacred Name, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (إلها) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (آخر) naʿt of إله, accusative; it is prevented from tanwīn because of being a descriptive adjective and the pattern أفعل (الفاء) the fāʾ of causation (fāʾ al-sababiyya) (تقعد) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the fāʾ, and the agent is "you" (مذموما) ḥāl, accusative (مخذولا) a second ḥāl, accusative..
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تقعد) is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to a maṣdar gleaned from the preceding prohibition, i.e.: "let there not be from you a setting up of a god with Allah, and then a sitting in a state of blame and abandonment".
The clause «لا تجعل ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «تقعد ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-type relative (أن).

* Morphology:
(مخذولا): a passive participle of the triliteral verb خذل; its pattern is مفعول.

safi-cedvel:23-24.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (قضى) a past verb, indeclinable on the implied fatḥa on the alif (ربّك) agent, nominative.. and (الكاف) is muḍāf ilayhi (أن) a maṣdar particle that governs the accusative [Note: or a particle lightened from the heavy (أنّ), its noun being an omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), i.e. "that it.."; (لا) is then a prohibitive that governs the jussive.], (لا) negative (تعبدوا) an imperfect verb, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the dropping of the nūn.. and (الواو) is the agent [Note: or jussive by the prohibitive لا, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn..] (إلّا) a particle of restriction [Note: or it is — on the second analysis — a particle of exception.], (إيّاه) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of the accusative, mafʿūl bihi [Note: or in the position of the accusative as the excepted, or a badal of the omitted object, i.e. "your Lord decreed that (it) you worship no one (أحدا) except Him".], (الواو) a conjunction (بالوالدين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "do good" (أحسنوا) (إحسانا) mafʿūl muṭlaq of the omitted verb, accusative [Note: see verses (83) of al-Baqara, (36) of al-Nisāʾ and (151) of al-Anʿām, for there is further detail about the i'rab of the word (إحسانا) and the place of attachment of the preposition (بالوالدين).]..
The interpreted maṣdar (ألا تعبدوا..) is in the position of the genitive by an omitted preposition, i.e. بألّا تعبدوا.., attached to (قضى).
(إن) a conditional particle that jussively governs (ما) redundant (يبلغنّ) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of the jussive of the condition.. and (النون) is for emphasis (عندك) an adverb, accusative, attached to (يبلغنّ), and (الكاف) is muḍāf ilayhi (الكبر) mafʿūl bihi, accusative (أحدهما) agent, nominative.. and (هما) is a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (أو) a conjunction (كلاهما) conjoined to أحدهما, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the alif, for it is appended to the dual, attached to the pronoun (الفاء) linking the apodosis (لا) a prohibitive that governs the jussive (تقل) an imperfect verb, jussive, and the agent is "you" (اللام) a preposition and (هما) an attached pronoun in the position of the genitive, attached to (تقل) (أفّ) a verbal noun (ism fiʿl) of the imperfect, meaning "I am vexed", and the agent is "I" (الواو) a conjunction (لا تنهر) like لا تقل.. and (هما) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (الواو) a conjunction (قل) an imperative verb, and the agent is "you" (لهما) like the first, attached to (قل) (قولا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative [Note: in the sense of "speech"; had the maṣdar been intended, it would be an accusative mafʿūl muṭlaq.], (كريما) naʿt of (قولا), accusative.
The clause «قضى ربّك ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «تعبدوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
The clause «إمّا يبلغنّ ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
The clause «لا تقل ... » is in the position of the jussive, as the apodosis accompanied by the fāʾ.
The clause «لا تنهرهما» is in the position of the jussive, conjoined to the clause لا تقل.
The clause «قل ... » is in the position of the jussive, conjoined to the clause لا تقل.
24- (الواو) a conjunction (اخفض لهما جناح) like قل لهما قولا.. and the preposition is attached to (اخفض) (الذلّ) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (من الرحمة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (اخفض) [Note: and مِن is causal or for the beginning of the limit, and it is permissible that the preposition be attached to an omitted ḥāl from جناح الذلّ.], (الواو) a conjunction (قل) like the first (ربّ) the one addressed (munādā), muḍāf, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied on what precedes the yāʾ that is dropped for lightness, and (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi (ارحمهما) like قل, and (هما) is a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the command is a supplication (الكاف) a preposition (ما) a maṣdar particle (ربّياني) a past verb, and (الألف) is the agent, and (النون) is for protection (wiqāya), and (الياء) is mafʿūl bihi (صغيرا) ḥāl from the yāʾ of the object, accusative..
The interpreted maṣdar (ما ربّياني) is in the position of the genitive by the kāf — which here has the sense of giving a reason, not of comparison — attached to (ارحم) [Note: for some the kāf is for comparison, so it is attached to a mafʿūl muṭlaq, and the implied form is: "have mercy on them with a mercy like their mercy to me" or "like their rearing of me".].
The clause «اخفض ... » is in the position of the jussive, conjoined to the clause لا تقل.
The clause «قل ... » is in the position of the jussive, conjoined to the clause لا تقل.
The clause «the vocative and its response ... » is in the position of the accusative, as the reported speech.
The clause «ارحمهما ... » has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
The clause «ربّياني ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (ما).

* Morphology:
(كلاهما): a noun indicating the dual whose form is singular, used for the masculine, always annexed.
(جناح): a rigid noun for the well-known organ; its pattern is فعال with a fatḥa on the fāʾ.
(الذلّ): a samāʿī maṣdar of the triliteral verb ذلّ; its pattern is فعل with a ḍamma then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
1- Istiʿāra makniyya and takhyīliyya (implicit and imaginative metaphor): in His saying, the Exalted: «وَاخْفِضْ لَهُما جَناحَ الذُّلِّ».
Humility is likened to a bird descending from on high, by an implicit simile; the wing is affirmed for it by imagination (takhyīl), and the lowering as a strengthening (tarshīḥ). For when a bird wants to fly and rise it spreads its wings and lifts them to ascend; when it leaves that, it lowers them. Also, when it sees a bird of prey it fears, it clings to the ground and presses its wings down, which is the extreme of its fear and humility. It has also been said that the lowering of them intended is what it does when it gathers its chicks, to rear them, and that this is more fitting to the context.

* Benefits:
1- Among the wonders of this language:
The grammarians differed about the verbal nouns (asmāʾ al-afʿāl) regarding their consideration and naming; the sound view is that they are verbal nouns and have no position in i'rab.
And «أف» is a verbal noun of the imperfect in the sense of «أتضجّر» ("I am vexed"). Its dialects are many, reaching, according to some, forty dialects, of which seven were recited, three of them mutawātir and four of the irregular (shādhdh) kind. In the reading of Ḥafṣ we read «أفّ» with kasra, tanwīn and shadda. If you are among the horsemen of this science, consult the longer works, for in them is what quenches the thirst of the thirsty.
2- Between contentment and disobedience (to parents):
After the reader has savoured the Qur'an's counsel to obey one's parents, it is fitting for us to mention a little of the story of those who were undutiful to their parents, for by contrast things are distinguished.
It is related that Jarīr was the most undutiful of people to his father. His son Bilāl was undutiful to him, and one day they reviled one another, and Bilāl was harsh to his father. His mother said to him: "O enemy of Allah, do you say this to your father?" Jarīr said: "Leave him; it is as though he heard it from me when I said it to my father."
Al-Ḥuṭayʾa was of notable undutifulness to parents; he said, satirising his father:
فنعم الشيخ أنت لدى المخازي ... وبئس الشيخ أنت لدى الفعال

جمعت اللؤم لا حياك ربي ... وأبواب السفاهة والضلال
(Gloss: "What a fine old man you are in disgraces, and what an evil old man you are in deeds; you have gathered baseness — may my Lord not greet you — and the doors of folly and error.")
And he said, satirising his mother:
لحاك الله ثم لحاك أمّا ... ولقاك العقوق من البنينا

أغربالا إذا استودعت سرّا ... وكانونا على المتحدثينا
(Gloss: "May Allah curse you, and again curse you as a mother, and may you meet undutifulness from sons; are you a sieve when entrusted with a secret, and a hearth over those who converse?")
